card.summary_ko: 최부(1454–1504)가 1487~88년 제주에서 풍랑을 만나 중국 저장성에 표착한 일을 쓴 일기 《표해록》의 첫 부분. 서문 격 보고, 출항 준비와 표류, 해적과 상륙, 도저소 심문, 닝보에서 샤오싱까지.
card.summary_en: The first part of Choe Bu's diary Pyohaerok (1488): his drift from Jeju to Zhejiang after a storm, the pirate attack, landfall, questioning at Taozhu, and the journey as far as Shaoxing. The Grand Canal stage is not included.
card.edition_ko: 중국어 위키문헌 「漂海錄」 (개정 2422207, 2024-06-15), 원저작 퍼블릭 도메인, 전사 CC BY-SA 4.0 — 卷01의 앞부분(서문 격 보고와 1487년 음력 9월 17일~1488년 음력 2월 4일 紹興 도착까지)만 수록. 紹興에서 끝나며 이후 항저우·대운하·북경 구간은 없음, 원문만·번역 없음
card.edition_en: Chinese Wikisource 「漂海錄」 (revision 2422207, 2024-06-15); original in the public domain, transcription CC BY-SA 4.0. Only the early part of juan 1 (the report-style preface and entries from the 17th of the 9th lunar month of 1487 to the 4th of the 2nd month of 1488, arrival at Shaoxing). The text ends at Shaoxing; Hangzhou, the Grand Canal and Beijing are not included. Original text only, no translation.

notes.ko:
**저자** 최부(1454–1504)는 전라도 나주 출신으로 호는 금남이며, 김종직의 문인입니다. 1477년 진사가 되고 1482년 문과에 급제해 성종 때 홍문관·사헌부 등에서 일한 사림 계열 관료입니다. 1487년 제주 추쇄경차관으로 파견되었다가 부친상 소식을 듣고 돌아오던 중 풍랑을 만나 중국 저장성에 표착했습니다. 훈구와 사림이 대립하던 시기에 사림에 속했고, 연산군 때인 1498년 무오사화에 연루되어 유배되었으며, 1504년 갑자사화에서 처형되었습니다. 외세에 협력했다거나 하는 문제는 없는 인물입니다.

**시대적 맥락** 1488년은 명 홍치제 초기로, 조선은 명과 사대 관계를 맺고 정기적으로 사신을 보내고 있었습니다. 최부 일행은 처음 왜구로 의심받았으나 조선 관료임을 입증해 항저우에서 대운하를 따라 베이징까지 호송된 뒤 요동을 거쳐 귀국했습니다. 그는 성종의 명으로 6개월의 여정을 일기로 정리해 올렸는데, 명의 지리, 풍속, 제도와 운하 교통을 자세히 기록했습니다. 이 책은 15세기 중국 강남을 외국인이 직접 본 귀중한 기록으로 평가되며, 일본과 서양 학계에서도 연구되었습니다. 이 기록 때문에 최부가 박해를 받은 것은 아닙니다.

**배경**
최부(崔溥, 1454–1504, 호 금남)는 성종 때 문신으로, 1487년 제주 추쇄경차관으로 파견되었다. 이듬해 정월 말(1488) 제주에서 부친상 소식을 듣고 윤정월 초 급히 뭍으로 향하다 풍랑을 만나 14일 동안 표류한 끝에 중국 저장성 해안에 닿았다. 일행은 43명이었다고 전한다. 중국 관리들은 처음에 왜구가 아닌가 의심했고, 최부는 신분을 밝혀 일행의 안전을 확보했다. 그는 항저우에서 대운하를 따라 북경까지 올라간 뒤 요동을 거쳐 귀국해 한양에 닿았고, 성종의 명으로 이 일기를 올렸다. 최부는 뒤에 1504년 갑자사화 때 처형되었다고 전한다.

**내용 (책 전체와 이 판)**
책은 3권이며, 날짜별 일기 형식으로 표류, 중국 상륙, 대운하 여행, 북경, 귀국 길까지를 기록한다. 이 판에는 卷01의 앞부분이 실려 있다.
- 서문 격 보고: 표류하다 닿은 일과 올린 사연.
- 1487년 음력 9월 17일~1488년 정월: 제주에 도착하고 부친상 소식, 출항 준비.
- 윤정월 3~16일: 거센 풍랑과 식수난, 선원들의 동요와 기도, 12일 해적을 만나 가진 것을 빼앗김, 16일 우두 외양(오늘의 저장성 린하이 일대)에 닿음.
- 17~22일: 상륙, 현지 주민과 관리들의 취조(桃渚所), 상복과 3년상 문답, 조사 진술서를 두고 오가는 말.
- 23일~2월 4일(음력): 건도소, 월계, 닝보, 츠시, 위야오, 상위를 거쳐 샤오싱에 이르기까지.
카탈로그가 약속한 ‘대운하를 따라 북경으로 가는 구간’은 이 판에 없다. 기록은 2월 4일 샤오싱(紹興) 도착에서 끝나며, 항저우 이후는 이 판에 없다.

**의의**
15세기 조선 관리가 직접 본 명나라 강남 사회의 사료로 높이 평가된다. 풍속, 지리, 관청 제도, 사람들의 반응이 날짜별로 자세하다.

**읽기 도움**
- 漂流: 바다에서 떠내려감. 喪人: 상중인 사람. 陪吏: 수행 아전.
- 推刷敬差官: 도망친 사람을 찾아내라고 보낸 임시 관리.
- 閏正月: 윤달인 1월.
- 倭: 왜구. 중국 관리가 일행을 의심한 이유.
- 千戶·把總官·總兵官: 명의 군 관직. 所·衛·巡檢司: 군사·치안 기관.
- 驛·鋪·橋: 역참, 숙소·초소, 다리. 虹門: 무지개 모양 아치.
- 大唐: 중국 사람들이 스스로를 일컬은 말.
- 招詞: 진술서. 轎: 가마.
- △: 날짜 앞에 붙은 표시. ——: 본문 안의 작은 풀이.
notes.en:
**About the author** Choe Bu (1454–1504), pen name Geumnam, came from Naju in Jeolla and was a pupil of Kim Jong-jik. He became a jinsa in 1477 and passed the civil examination in 1482, serving under King Seongjong in the Office of Special Advisors, the Office of the Inspector-General and elsewhere, as an official of the Sarim camp. Sent to Jeju in 1487 as a commissioner for tracking down runaways, he was returning on news of his father's death when a storm drove him ashore in Zhejiang, China. In the rivalry between the Hungu and the Sarim he stood with the Sarim, was implicated in the Muo literati purge of 1498 under Yeonsangun and exiled, and was executed in the Gapja purge of 1504.

**Historical context** In 1488, early in the Hongzhi reign, Joseon was a Ming tributary state sending regular envoys. Choe Bu's party was first suspected of being Japanese pirates, but he proved his status as a Joseon official; they were escorted from Hangzhou up the Grand Canal to Beijing and returned via Liaodong. By King Seongjong's order he wrote up the journey as a diary, recording Ming geography, customs, institutions and canal transport in detail. It is valued as a rare first-hand foreign account of 15th-century Jiangnan China and has been studied by scholars in Japan and the West. The record was not the cause of his later persecution.

**Background**
Choe Bu (1454-1504, pen name Geumnam) was an official under King Seongjong, sent to Jeju in 1487 as a commissioner to track down runaways. At the end of the first month of 1488 he heard on Jeju of his father's death, and early in the leap first month he set out for the mainland in haste; a storm drove him adrift for 14 days until he reached the coast of Zhejiang. His party, traditionally 43 people, was first suspected of being Japanese pirates, and Choe Bu proved his status to secure their safety. He was taken from Hangzhou up the Grand Canal to Beijing, then back through Liaodong to Hanyang, and wrote this diary by royal command. He was later executed, it is said, in the 1504 purge.

**Contents (whole book and this edition)**
The book has three juan in dated diary form: the drift, landfall in China, the canal journey, Beijing and the road home. This edition contains the early part of juan 1.
- A report-style preface on the drift and the diary.
- 17th of the 9th lunar month 1487 to the first month 1488: arrival at Jeju, news of the father's death, preparations to sail.
- Leap first month, 3rd-16th: fierce seas, water shortage, the crew's panic and prayers, a pirate attack on the 12th that strips them of belongings, landfall on the 16th off Niutou, in the Linhai area of today's Zhejiang.
- 17th-22nd: landing, questioning by locals and officers (Taozhu), the exchange about mourning dress and three-year mourning, and discussion of the statement he must write.
- 23rd to the 4th of the 2nd month (lunar): via Jiantiao, Yuexi, Ningbo, Cixi, Yuyao and Shangyu to Shaoxing.
The Grand Canal stage to Beijing promised in the catalogue is not in this edition: the text ends on the 4th of the 2nd month with the arrival at Shaoxing, and nothing after that (Hangzhou onward) is included.

**Significance**
It is prized as a first-hand account by a fifteenth-century Joseon official of Ming-era Jiangnan: customs, geography, officialdom and people's reactions, day by day.

**Reading help**
- 漂流: to drift at sea; 喪人: person in mourning; 陪吏: accompanying clerk.
- 推刷敬差官: special commissioner sent to trace runaways.
- 閏正月: the leap first month.
- 倭: Japanese pirates, why the officials suspected the party.
- 千戶, 把總官, 總兵官: Ming military ranks; 所, 衛, 巡檢司: garrison and policing posts.
- 驛, 鋪, 橋: relay station, post-house or checkpoint, bridge; 虹門: arched gate.
- 大唐: what local people called their own country.
- 招詞: written statement; 轎: sedan chair.
- △ before dates; —— marks small inline notes.

paragraphs.en: Book 1

paragraphs.orig: 喪人臣崔溥，自濟州漂流，泊甌東，過越南，經燕北，以今六月十四日到青坡驛。敬奉傳旨，一行日錄撰集以進。
paragraphs.reading: 상인신최부, 자제주표류, 박구동, 과월남, 경연북, 이금유월십사일도청파역. 경봉전지, 일행일록찬집이진.
paragraphs.en: I, Choe Bu, a man in mourning and your servant, drifted from Jeju, anchored in the east of Ou (Oudong), passed through the south of Yue (Yuenan), and went by way of the north of Yan (Yanbei); on the fourteenth day of the sixth month of this year I arrived at Cheongpa Station. Respectfully receiving the royal command, I have compiled this record of the daily events of the whole journey and present it.

paragraphs.orig: ## △成化二十三年丁未秋九月十七日
paragraphs.en: Chenghua 23rd year (dingwei), autumn, 9th month, 17th day

paragraphs.orig: 臣以濟州三邑推刷敬差官陛辭而行，至全羅道，率監司依事目所差光州牧吏程保、和順縣吏金重及承仕郎李楨、羅州隨陪吏孫孝子、青岩驛吏崔巨伊山、戶奴萬山等六人及司僕寺安驥、崔根等，歸海南縣候風。
paragraphs.reading: 신이제주삼읍추쇄경차관폐사이행, 지전라도, 솔감사의사목소차광주목리정보, 화순현리김중급승사랑이정, 나주수배리손효자, 청암역리최거이산, 호노만산등육인급사복사안기, 최근등, 귀해남현후풍.
paragraphs.en: I, as Special Commissioner for the investigation and recall of the people of the three districts of Jeju, took formal leave of the king at the palace steps and set out. On reaching Jeolla Province, I took with me, as appointed by the Provincial Governor in accordance with the written instructions: Jeong Bo, a clerk of Gwangju Prefecture; Kim Jung, a clerk of Hwasun County; Yi Jeong, holder of the rank of Seungsarang; Son Hyoja, an attendant clerk of Naju; Choe Geoisan, a clerk of Cheongam Station; and Mansan, a household slave — six men in all — together with An Gi and Choe Geun of the Saboksi (Court of the Royal Stables). We returned to Haenam County to wait for a favourable wind.

paragraphs.orig: ## △十一月十一日
paragraphs.en: 11th month, 11th day

paragraphs.orig: 朝，與濟州新牧使許熙同乘舟於館頭梁。
paragraphs.reading: 조, 여제주신목사허희동승주어관두량.
paragraphs.en: In the morning, together with Heo Hui, the newly appointed Magistrate of Jeju, I boarded a ship at Gwanduryang.

paragraphs.orig: ## △十二日
paragraphs.en: 12th day

paragraphs.orig: 夕，到泊濟州朝天館。
paragraphs.reading: 석, 도박제주조천관.
paragraphs.en: In the evening we arrived and anchored at the Jocheon Lodge in Jeju.

paragraphs.orig: ## △弘治元年戊申正月三十日
paragraphs.en: Hongzhi 1st year (wushen), 1st month, 30th day

paragraphs.orig: 陰。晡時，臣之奴莫金自羅州到濟州，齎喪服來告臣父之喪。
paragraphs.reading: 음. 포시, 신지노막금자나주도제주, 재상복래고신부지상.
paragraphs.en: Overcast. In the late afternoon my slave Makgeum arrived in Jeju from Naju, bringing mourning clothes, and came to tell me of the death of my father.

paragraphs.orig: ## △閏正月初一日
paragraphs.en: Intercalary 1st month, 1st day

paragraphs.orig: 雨。牧使晨夕來弔，乃以水精寺僧智慈之船牢固疾行，官船所不及，命兵房鎮撫高益堅、吳純等回泊於別刀浦，以為臣渡海之備。判官鄭銓遣軍官邊石山以弔。
paragraphs.reading: 우. 목사신석래조, 내이수정사승지자지선뇌고질행, 관선소불급, 명병방진무고익견, 오순등회박어별도포, 이위신도해지비. 판관정전견군관변석산이조.
paragraphs.en: Rain. The Magistrate came morning and evening to offer condolences. Then, because the boat of the monk Jija of Sujeongsa Temple was sturdy and fast, such that government ships could not match it, he ordered the pacification officers of the Military Section, Go Ikgyeon, O Sun and others, to bring it back and anchor it at Byeoldopo, in preparation for my crossing of the sea. The Assistant Magistrate, Jeong Jeon, sent the military officer Byeon Seoksan to offer condolences.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初二日
paragraphs.en: 2nd day

paragraphs.orig: 陰。侵晨，臣詣別刀浦候風館。旌義縣訓導崔角、鄉校生徒金鼎璘等二十餘輩、內需司典會朴重幹及崔根等，皆徒步以隨至十五里許。少選，牧使馳至問慰。是日，臣之帶去吏程保、金重等，封所治采御乘監牧場辦公私賤、刷流移人——括濫占伴倘、冒認良民——等文籍及齎去全州府上濟州三邑帳籍十七冊，又一冊濟州三邑官上各年帳、戶籍、軍籍等文書，輸付於牧使，藏之營廳，受書目回送而來。
paragraphs.reading: 음. 침신, 신예별도포후풍관. 정의현훈도최각, 향교생도김정린등이십여배, 내수사전회박중간급최근등, 개도보이수지십오리허. 소선, 목사치지문위. 시일, 신지대거리정보, 김중등, 봉소치채어승감목장판공사천, 쇄유이인——괄남점반당, 모인양민——등문적급재거전주부상제주삼읍장적십칠책, 우일책제주삼읍관상각년장, 호적, 군적등문서, 수부어목사, 장지영청, 수서목회송이래.
paragraphs.en: Overcast. At first light I went to the Wind-Waiting Lodge at Byeoldopo. Choe Gak, instructor of Jeongui County; Kim Jeongrin and other students of the local school, twenty or more in all; Bak Junggan, Superintendent of the Naesusa; and Choe Geun and others all followed me on foot for about fifteen li. Shortly afterwards the Magistrate galloped up to console me. That day the clerks Jeong Bo, Kim Jung and the others who had come with me sealed up the documents they had been handling — the records concerning the sorting out of public and private slaves at the pastures of the royal-mount supervisory office, and the rounding up of vagrants and migrants (namely, the registration of those wrongfully held as retainers and those falsely passing themselves off as commoners) and the like; the seventeen volumes of the household registers of the three districts of Jeju that had been brought from Jeonju Prefecture; and one further volume of annual registers, household registers, military registers and other documents of the offices of the three districts of Jeju. They handed these over to the Magistrate to be stored in the government office, received a written receipt, and came back.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初三日
paragraphs.en: 3rd day

paragraphs.orig: 漂流海中。是日乍陰乍雨，東風微順。海色深青。大靜縣監鄭嗣瑞、訓導盧警聞臣遇喪，馳來弔慰。與崔角、朴重幹、倭學訓導金繼郁、軍官崔仲眾、鎮撫金仲理等十餘人，學長金存麗、金得禮、校生二十餘輩，俱送別於浦口。存麗、得禮等止臣行，曰：「老僕生長海國，諳經水路。漢拏山陰雨不調必有風變，不可乘船。且《家禮》『始聞親喪遂行』註云：『日行百里不夜行，雖哀戚猶避害也。』夜行尚不可，況過此大海，其可不慎乎？」座中或勸或止，日高不決。鎮撫安義來告曰：「東風正好，可以去矣！」重幹、仲眾等亦勸行。臣遂告別登船。棹過五里，軍人權山、許尚理等皆曰：「今日風勢若作若輟，雲霾若卷若舒，當如此風候不順之日，行如此波濤險惡之海，恐有後悔。請還於別刀浦，待風復行未為晚也。」安義曰：「天之氣候，非人預料，頃刻之間，安知有披雲睹天之理乎？抑過此海者，私船覆沒接踵相繼，唯奉王命朝臣、前旌義縣監李暹外，鮮有漂流敗沒者，則都是上德至重，實天所知也。況謀之眾口，事未有濟。豈可登程而復路，以致稽緩乎！」叱令張帆而行。才過大火脫島，舟中人皆以謂：「舟向巨要梁，截海而上，順風泊楸子島，甚駛也。」權山不聽其言，執其舵，從風所指，過愁德島而西。海氣晦冥，風弱雨作。將近楸子島藏船處，汐勢甚急，天又昏黑，督令格軍櫓之。軍人皆曰：「若此日發船誰之過歟？」皆懷逆心，不聽從，以力櫓，退流至草蘭島，依西岸下碇而泊。夜三更，尚理曰：「此島雖礙東風，三面通闊，不合泊船。今又有北風之漸，進退無據，將奈何？且此船不在初泊處，漸卻入海中，所泊之碇怕或已破。今計莫若舉碇稍前繫之於岸，待天明棹入楸子可也。」遂舉碇，果破矣。棹之，未及近岸，為北風所逆，驅出無依之處。雨猶不止，風浪交惡，隨濤上下，莫知所適。
paragraphs.reading: 표류해중. 시일사음사우, 동풍미순. 해색심청. 대정현감정사서, 훈도노경문신우상, 치래조위. 여최각, 박중간, 왜학훈도김계욱, 군관최중중, 진무김중리등십여인, 학장김존려, 김득례, 교생이십여배, 구송별어포구. 존려, 득례등지신행, 왈: 「노복생장해국, 암경수로. 한라산음우부조필유풍변, 불가승선. 차《가례》『시문친상수행』주운: 『일행백리불야행, 수애척유피해야. 』야행상불가, 황과차대해, 기가불신호?」좌중혹권혹지, 일고불결. 진무안의래고왈: 「동풍정호, 가이거의!」중간, 중중등역권행. 신수고별등선. 도과오리, 군인권산, 허상리등개왈: 「금일풍세약작약철, 운매약권약서, 당여차풍후불순지일, 행여차파도험오지해, 공유후회. 청환어별도포, 대풍부행미위만야.」안의왈: 「천지기후, 비인예료, 경각지간, 안지유피운도천지리호? 억과차해자, 사선복몰접종상계, 유봉왕명조신, 전정의현감이섬외, 선유표류패몰자, 칙도시상덕지중, 실천소지야. 황모지중구, 사미유제. 기가등정이복로, 이치계완호!」질영장범이행. 재과대화탈도, 주중인개이위: 「주향거요량, 절해이상, 순풍박추자도, 심사야.」권산불청기언, 집기타, 종풍소지, 과수덕도이서. 해기회명, 풍약우작. 장근추자도장선처, 석세심급, 천우혼흑, 독영격군로지. 군인개왈: 「약차일발선수지과여?」개회역심, 불청종, 이력로, 퇴류지초란도, 의서안하정이박. 야삼경, 상리왈: 「차도수애동풍, 삼면통활, 불합박선. 금우유북풍지점, 진퇴무거, 장내하? 차차선부재초박처, 점각입해중, 소박지정파혹이파. 금계막약거정초전계지어안, 대천명도입추자가야.」수거정, 과파의. 도지, 미급근안, 위북풍소역, 구출무의지처. 우유부지, 풍랑교악, 수도상하, 막지소적.
paragraphs.en: Drifting at sea. That day it was by turns overcast and rainy, with a gentle and favourable east wind. The colour of the sea was deep blue. Jeong Saseo, Magistrate of Daejeong County, and the instructor No Gyeong, hearing that I had met with a bereavement, galloped over to condole with me and console me. Together with Choe Gak, Bak Junggan, Kim Gyeuk, instructor of Japanese studies, the military officer Choe Jungjung, the pacification officer Kim Jungni and others — ten or more in all — and the school heads Kim Jonnyeo and Kim Deukrye with some twenty students, they all saw me off at the harbour mouth. Jonnyeo, Deukrye and the others tried to stop my journey, saying: “We old servants were born and raised in a maritime land and know the sea routes well. The dark rain on Mt. Hallasan is unsettled, and there is sure to be a change of wind; you must not board a ship. Moreover, on the passage in the Family Rites, ‘On first hearing of a parent’s death, set out at once,’ the commentary says: ‘Travel a hundred li a day and do not travel by night; though in grief, one still avoids harm.’ If even night travel is not allowed, how much less crossing this great sea — can you be anything but careful?” Among those present, some urged me to go and some to stop, and when the sun was high we had still not decided. The pacification officer An Ui came and said: “The east wind is just right; we can go!” Junggan, Jungjung and others also urged me to set out. I then took my leave and boarded the boat. After we had rowed five li, the soldiers Gwon San, Heo Sangni and others all said: “Today the wind comes and goes, the clouds gather and part. On a day when the wind is so unfavourable, to travel over so dangerous and wild a sea, we fear you will regret it. Let us return to Byeoldopo and wait for the wind to turn again; it would not be too late.” An Ui said: “The weather of Heaven cannot be foreseen by men; in a moment, who knows that there will not be a parting of the clouds and a sight of the sky? Moreover, among those who cross this sea, private boats capsize and sink one after another; apart from envoys bearing the king’s command, court officials, and the former Jeongui County Magistrate Yi Seom, scarcely any have drifted and been lost, which shows that the royal virtue is of the utmost weight, and Heaven truly knows it. Besides, if we consult the many mouths, nothing ever gets done. How can we set out and then turn back, and so cause delay!” He scolded them and ordered the sail raised, and we went on. We had just passed Daehwaltal Island when the people in the boat all said: “The boat is heading for Georyoryang, cutting across the sea to the north; with a following wind we shall put in at Chuja Island — a very fast run.” Gwon San would not listen to them but took the rudder himself and, following where the wind pointed, passed Sudeok Island and went west. The sea air was dark, the wind weak, and rain began. As we approached the place at Chuja Island where boats are kept, the tide was running very fast and the sky had also grown black, and he ordered the rowers to ply the sweeps. The soldiers all said: “If we sail on a day like this, whose fault is it?” They all harboured a rebellious heart and would not obey; but they rowed with all their strength, and were swept back to Choran Island, where we dropped anchor on the west shore and moored. At the third watch of the night Sangni said: “This island, though it shelters us from the east wind, is open on three sides and not fit to moor a ship. Now, too, there is a hint of north wind coming. We can neither advance nor retreat; what are we to do? Besides, the boat is no longer at the place where we first anchored but is gradually being drawn back out to sea; I fear the anchor we moored with may already be broken. My reckoning now is that the best course is to raise the anchor, move a little forward and tie up to the shore, and at daybreak row into Chuja; that would do.” They raised the anchor, and it had indeed broken. We rowed, but before we could get near the shore the north wind met us head-on and drove us out to a place with nothing to rely on. The rain still did not stop, wind and waves were both bad, and we rose and fell with the swells, not knowing where we were going.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初四日
paragraphs.en: 4th day

paragraphs.orig: 漂入大洋中。是日雨雹，大風。驚濤畏浪，掀天鼓海，帆席盡破。舟以二檣高大尤易傾撓，勢將覆壓！命肖斤寶操斧去之。高以福縛草芚附之舟尾以禦濤。當午，雨稍霽，東風又大作，載傾載浮，聽其所之。瞥眼間，已入西海。梢工指東北，望有島——若一點彈丸於漂渺間，——曰：「彼疑乃黑山島也。」過此以往，四無島嶼，水天相接。汗漫無涯之海，人皆罔知攸措，僵臥舟中。臣令安義督軍人以取露治船等事。有軍人高迴者，作聲曰：「濟州海路甚險，凡往來者，皆待風累朔，至如前敬差官在朝天館，在水精寺，通計凡三朔以候，然後乃行。今此行，當風雨不定之時，不占一日之候，以至此極，皆自取也。」餘軍皆曰：「勢已如此！取露治船，雖竭心力終亦必亡。吾與其用力而死，莫如安臥以待死。」皆掩耳不從命，或毆之亦不起。宋真——孱劣之甚者——被毆而怒曰：「長壽哉！此船也。等至於破，何不速破！」程保曰：「濟州人心外癡內毒，頑慢戾悍，以死為輕，故其言類如此。」臣意亦以謂溺死已決矣。
paragraphs.reading: 표입대양중. 시일우박, 대풍. 경도외랑, 흔천고해, 범석진파. 주이이장고대우이경요, 세장복압! 명초근보조부거지. 고이복박초둔부지주미이어도. 당오, 우초제, 동풍우대작, 재경재부, 청기소지. 별안간, 이입서해. 초공지동북, 망유도——약일점탄환어표묘간, ——왈: 「피의내흑산도야.」과차이왕, 사무도서, 수천상접. 한만무애지해, 인개망지유조, 강와주중. 신영안의독군인이취로치선등사. 유군인고회자, 작성왈: 「제주해로심험, 범왕래자, 개대풍누삭, 지여전경차관재조천관, 재수정사, 통계범삼삭이후, 연후내행. 금차행, 당풍우부정지시, 부점일일지후, 이지차극, 개자취야.」여군개왈: 「세이여차! 취로치선, 수갈심력종역필망. 오여기용력이사, 막여안와이대사.」개엄이부종명, 혹구지역불기. 송진——잔렬지심자——피구이노왈: 「장수재! 차선야. 등지어파, 하불속파!」정보왈: 「제주인심외치내독, 완만려한, 이사위경, 고기언유여차.」신의역이위익사이결의.
paragraphs.en: Drifted into the open ocean. That day there was rain and hail and a great wind. Terrifying breakers and fearsome waves heaved at the sky and churned the sea, and the sail-mats were all torn. Because the boat’s two masts were tall and heavy and especially liable to make her heel and twist, she seemed about to capsize and be crushed! I ordered So Geunbo to take an axe and cut them away. Go Ibok bound straw matting and fastened it to the stern of the boat to hold off the waves. At noon the rain eased somewhat, but the east wind rose again strongly; the boat now heeled, now floated, and we let her go where she would. In the twinkling of an eye we had already entered the Western Sea. The helmsman pointed to the north-east, and we saw an island — like a single pellet in the hazy distance — and he said: “That seems to be Heuksan Island.” Beyond this there were no islands, and sea and sky joined. On the boundless, endless sea, everyone was at a loss what to do, and lay stiff in the boat. I ordered An Ui to supervise the soldiers in bailing and in the other work of keeping the boat in order. A soldier named Go Hoe raised his voice and said: “The sea route from Jeju is extremely dangerous. All who come and go wait for a wind for months on end; as for the former Special Commissioner, who waited at the Jocheon Lodge and at Sujeongsa, all told he waited three months before leaving. Now this time, at a moment when wind and rain were unsettled, without waiting even a single day for the weather, we have come to this extremity; we have brought it on ourselves.” The rest of the soldiers all said: “It is already like this! Bailing and mending the boat, even if we exhaust our hearts and strength, we are bound to die in the end. Rather than die using our strength, better to lie down in peace and wait for death.” They all covered their ears and would not obey orders; even when some were beaten they did not get up. Song Jin — the frailest and weakest of them — being beaten, said in anger: “Long-lived indeed, this boat! If it is going to break up in the end, why doesn’t it break up at once!” Jeong Bo said: “The people of Jeju are foolish on the outside and cruel within; they are stubborn, lazy, perverse and fierce, and think lightly of death — that is why they talk like this.” I too thought that death by drowning was already settled.

paragraphs.orig: 倘蒙天助，幸不至於溺，必漂流無定，以至死日，無如之何？又憤軍人怠惰，遂點檢同舟人，則從者程保、金重、李楨、孫孝子、崔巨伊山、莫金、萬山及濟州牧使所定送鎮撫安義，記官李孝枝，總牌許尚理，領船權山，梢工金高面，格軍金怪山、肖斤寶、金仇叱迴、玄山、金石貴、高以福、金朝回、文迴、李孝台、姜有、夫命同、高內乙同、高福、宋真、金都終、韓每山、鄭實，護送軍金粟、金真音山、高迴、金松、高保終、梁達海、朴終回、金得時、任山海，官奴權松、姜內、李山、吳山等，合自身，凡四十三人。臣招安義，問曰：「我一喪人，非官員例，從者至煩，甚為未便。濟州人乘船者，至三十五人，何也？」安義曰：「我牧使所以盡心者，待以敬差官之禮。且運大船必用眾力然後可行。況海路敻遠，如於蔚島等處水賊盛行，護送不可不嚴也。」臣曰：「過海時，當精擇運船人及水路諳習者，則數雖少可矣。今此同舟人皆懈怠暴盩者，虛張名數而無其實，使船漂流致之死地，徒增痛哭耳。」叫謂軍人等曰：「我奔初喪，情不可少留，人或有勸之行。為人子者，其可頃刻濡滯乎？汝等之同我見漂，實由於我，然勢亦使之然也。況好生惡死人情所同，汝等豈無欲生之心哉？舟或破碎或沉覆則已矣。觀舟今堅致，未易至破，若不遇石嶼，能修補刮水，幸或風定波恬，則雖流至他國可以得生。今汝等亦有父母，有妻兒，有昆季、親戚，皆望汝生，畏其不壽。汝等不念其情，不愛其身，徒以咎我之心率相解體，自歸死地，惑之甚者！」尚理等十餘人曰：「軍人皆頑鈍無識之徒，故其用心不通若此。然人各有心，我等各竭力從事，斃而後已。」夜，風雨不止，巨濤尤甚，激入舶艫，隨入隨取。

paragraphs.en: Even if, by the help of Heaven, we were by good fortune not to drown, we should surely drift without direction until the day of our deaths; what could be done? I was furthermore angry at the soldiers’ laziness, and so I took a count of those on board. They were: my attendants Jeong Bo, Kim Jung, Yi Jeong, Son Hyoja, Choe Geoisan, Makgeum and Mansan; those assigned by the Magistrate of Jeju — the pacification officer An Ui, the record-keeper Yi Hyoji, the squad leader Heo Sangni, the ship’s captain Gwon San, and the helmsman Kim Gomyeon; the crew (gyeokgun) Kim Goesan, So Geunbo, Kim Gujilhoe, Hyeonsan, Kim Seokgwi, Go Ibok, Kim Johoe, Mun Hoe, Yi Hyotae, Gang Yu, Bu Myeongdong, Go Naeuldong, Go Bok, Song Jin, Kim Dojong, Han Maesan and Jeong Sil; the escort soldiers Kim Sok, Kim Jineumsan, Go Hoe, Kim Song, Go Bojong, Yang Dalhae, Bak Jonghoe, Kim Deuksi and Im Sanhae; and the government slaves Gwon Song, Gang Nae, Yi San and O San — together with myself, forty-three persons in all. I summoned An Ui and asked: “I am a man in mourning, not of the class of an official; to have so many attendants is very inconvenient. Why do as many as thirty-five Jeju men travel by ship?” An Ui said: “The reason our Magistrate took such pains is that he treated you with the courtesy due to a Special Commissioner. Moreover, to handle a large ship you must have many hands before it can go. And the sea route is distant; in places like Uldo, water-bandits are rife, so the escort cannot but be strict.” I said: “When crossing the sea, you should have carefully chosen men to work the ship and men familiar with the sea routes; then, though the number were small, it would be enough. Now the people on this boat are all slack, lazy, wild and perverse; they inflate the count with names without substance, and let the boat drift to a place of death. This adds nothing but grief.” Calling to the soldiers, I said: “I am hurrying to my father’s fresh mourning; in feeling I could not wait even a little, and some people urged me to go. For a son, could I linger for even a moment? That you drifted with me is really because of me, but circumstances also made it so. Moreover, loving life and hating death is what all men’s feelings share; do you not have a wish to live? If the boat breaks up or sinks, that will be the end. But I see the boat is sturdy now and not easily broken; if we do not meet rocky islets, can mend it and bail out the water, and by luck the wind settles and the waves grow calm, then even if we drift to another country we can live. You too have parents, wives and children, brothers and relatives, all hoping you will live and fearing that you will not reach your years. If you do not think of their feelings and do not cherish your own bodies, and merely out of resentment against me lead one another into slackness, going of your own accord to a place of death — that is a great delusion!” Sangni and some ten others said: “The soldiers are all stubborn, dull and ignorant, so their thinking does not reach this far. But each man has his own heart; we shall each exert our strength in the work, until we fall dead.” At night the wind and rain did not cease, and the huge waves grew worse, surging into the hull; as fast as the water came in, we bailed it out.

paragraphs.orig: 量可二更，驚濤鼓蕩，襄駕篷屋。舟半沉，衣服、行李盡見沾濡。凍寒砭骨，命在瞬息。臣握李楨手，枕程保膝。金重、孝子傍臣左右，狼藉以待死。旁有一人結項將絕。李楨解其絕，則乃吳山也。巨伊山、莫金等竭力汲水，水猶不減。臣以謂舟尚完固，則自上激射、自隙漏入之水，不汲則坐待沉沒，汲之則庶有生理。勉強而起，叫權松攢燧得火，卷芚席以烘之。又叫斤寶、高福、高面等親檢罅漏處，以補塞之。又解衣分給權山、高面、巨伊山、怪山、尚理等，以勸勉所事。程保、金重、孝子等亦散衣服分諸軍人。軍人若仇叱迴、文迴、都終、每山、玄山等爭感奮出，死力刮水殆盡，舟僅獲全。不移時，舟又入石嶼錯亂中，權山運船不知所向。尚理、仇叱迴等執篙無所施。幸賴天風驅出，得免碎破。

paragraphs.en: At about the second watch, terrifying waves surged and raged, sweeping over the awning and the mat roof. The boat was half sunk; clothes and baggage were all soaked through. The freezing cold pierced to the bone, and life hung on a moment. I gripped Yi Jeong’s hand and laid my head on Jeong Bo’s knee. Kim Jung and Hyoja lay at my left and right, in a heap, awaiting death. Nearby, a man had tied a noose round his neck and was close to the end. Yi Jeong undid the rope — it was O San. Geoisan, Makgeum and the others bailed with all their strength, but the water did not go down. I reasoned that while the boat was still sound, the water dashing down from above and leaking in through the seams would, if not bailed, mean sitting and waiting for the boat to sink, whereas if bailed there was hope of life. Forcing myself up, I called Gwon Song to strike a flint and get fire, and to roll up the matting and dry it. I also called Geunbo, Go Bok, Gomyeon and others to inspect the cracks and leaks themselves and stop them up. I also took off clothes and gave them to Gwon San, Gomyeon, Geoisan, Goesan, Sangni and the others, to encourage them in their tasks. Jeong Bo, Kim Jung, Hyoja and the rest also distributed clothes among the soldiers. The soldiers such as Gujilhoe, Mun Hoe, Dojong, Maesan and Hyeonsan vied with one another in being moved and roused, and bailed with all their might until the water was almost gone, and the boat was barely saved. Before long the boat again ran into a confusion of rocky islets, and Gwon San, steering, did not know the direction. Sangni, Gujilhoe and the others took up poles but could do nothing with them. By good fortune a wind from heaven drove us out, and we escaped being smashed to pieces.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初五日
paragraphs.en: 5th day

paragraphs.orig: 漂大洋中。是日昏霧四塞，咫尺不辨。向晚，雨腳如麻。至夜，雨少止，怒濤如山，高若出青天，下若入深淵，犇衝擊躍，聲裂天地。胥溺臭敗，決在呼吸之間。莫金、權松等抆淚胃臣曰：「勢已迫矣！無復望已，請替換衣服，以待大命之至。」臣如其言，懷印與馬牌，具喪冠與服，惴惴然挼手祝天曰：「臣在世唯忠孝友愛為心，心無欺罔，身無仇冤，手無殺害，天雖高高，實所鑒臨。今又奉君命而往，奔父喪而歸。臣不知有何罪咎？倘臣有罪，罰及臣身可也。同舟四十餘人無罪見溺，天其敢不矜憐乎？天若哀此窮人，返風息濤，使臣得再生於世，葬臣新死之父，養臣垂老之母，幸又得鞠躬於丹墀之下，然後雖萬死無生，臣實甘心。」言未訖，莫金遽抱臣身曰：「一家人百年苦樂皆仰此身，有如十盲仰一杖。今至於此，無復再見一家之人！」遂擗踊而哭。陪吏以下亦哭泣，攢手以祈天祜。
paragraphs.reading: 표대양중. 시일혼무사색, 지척불변. 향만, 우각여마. 지야, 우소지, 노도여산, 고약출청천, 하약입심연, 분충격약, 성렬천지. 서닉취패, 결재호흡지간. 막금, 권송등문루위신왈: 「세이박의! 무부망이, 청체환의복, 이대대명지지.」신여기언, 회인여마패, 구상관여복, 췌췌연뇌수축천왈: 「신재세유충효우애위심, 심무기망, 신무구원, 수무살해, 천수고고, 실소감임. 금우봉군명이왕, 분부상이귀. 신부지유하죄구? 당신유죄, 벌급신신가야. 동주사십여인무죄견닉, 천기감불긍련호? 천약애차궁인, 반풍식도, 사신득재생어세, 장신신사지부, 양신수로지모, 행우득국궁어단지지하, 연후수만사무생, 신실감심.」언미흘, 막금거포신신왈: 「일가인백년고락개앙차신, 유여십맹앙일장. 금지어차, 무부재견일가지인!」수벽용이곡. 배리이하역곡읍, 찬수이기천호.
paragraphs.en: Drifting in the open ocean. That day thick fog closed in on all sides, and one could not make out things an inch before the eyes. Towards evening the rain fell like threads of hemp. At night the rain eased a little; angry waves like mountains, high as though rising out of the blue sky and low as though plunging into an abyss, charged, struck and leapt, their sound splitting heaven and earth. Being drowned and rotted and ruined was decided within the space of a breath. Makgeum, Gwon Song and the others wiped away their tears and said to me: “It is pressing upon us now! There is no hope any more; please change your clothes and wait for the great decree to arrive.” I did as they said: I held my seal and horse-tablet to my breast, put on the mourning cap and garments, and, trembling, clasping my hands, prayed to Heaven: “In life your servant has had only loyalty, filial piety, friendship and love in his heart; there is no deceit in my heart, no enmity in my person, no killing in my hands; Heaven, though high, truly looks down. Now I went on the king’s command, and I return hastening to my father’s funeral. I do not know what offence I have committed. If your servant has sinned, let the punishment fall on my own body. That the forty or so men in this boat, guiltless, should be drowned — would Heaven dare not to pity them? If Heaven has compassion on this man in extremity, turn the wind, still the waves, let your servant have a second life in this world, bury my newly dead father, nourish my aged mother, and by good fortune bow once more before the vermilion steps of the palace; then, even if I should die ten thousand deaths with no life remaining, your servant would be truly content.” Before I had finished speaking, Makgeum suddenly threw his arms round my body and said: “The joys and sorrows of a whole household for a hundred years depend upon this one body, as ten blind men depend on one staff. Now it has come to this, and we shall never see the people of our household again!” And beating his breast and stamping his feet, he wept. The attendant clerks and the others also wept, and joined hands to pray for Heaven’s blessing.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初六日
paragraphs.en: 6th day

paragraphs.orig: 漂大洋中。是日陰，風波少歇。始督仇叱迴等葺片席以為帆，建桅竿以為檣，劈舊檣之木以為碇，隨風西向而去。顧見洪濤間有物，不知其大也。其見於水上者，如長屋廊，噴沫射天，波翻浪駭。梢工戒舟人，搖手令勿語。舟過甚遠然後梢工呼曰：「彼乃鯨也！大則吞航，小能覆舟，今幸不相值，我其更生，更生矣！」入夜，風濤還勁，舟行甚疾。安義曰：「嘗聞海有龍神，甚貪，請投行李有物，以禳謝之。」臣不之應。舟人皆曰：「人有此身，然後有此物，此物皆身外物。」爭檢有染衣服、軍器、鐵器、口糧等物投諸海。臣亦莫之能禁。
paragraphs.reading: 표대양중. 시일음, 풍파소헐. 시독구질회등즙편석이위범, 건외간이위장, 벽구장지목이위정, 수풍서향이거. 고견홍도간유물, 부지기대야. 기견어수상자, 여장옥랑, 분말사천, 파번랑해. 초공계주인, 요수영물어. 주과심원연후초공호왈: 「피내경야! 대칙탄항, 소능복주, 금행불상치, 아기갱생, 갱생의!」입야, 풍도환경, 주행심질. 안의왈: 「상문해유용신, 심탐, 청투행리유물, 이양사지.」신부지응. 주인개왈: 「인유차신, 연후유차물, 차물개신외물.」쟁검유염의복, 군기, 철기, 구량등물투제해. 신역막지능금.
paragraphs.en: Drifting in the open ocean. That day overcast; the wind and waves abated a little. First I ordered Gujilhoe and the others to patch scraps of mat into a sail, to set up a pole as the mast, and to split the wood of the old mast to make an anchor; and we went west with the wind. Looking back, we saw something among the great waves, its size unknown. What showed above the water was like a long gallery of a house, spouting spray into the sky, the waves tumbling and the surf alarmed. The helmsman warned the people on the boat, waving his hand to tell them not to speak. When the boat had gone a long way past, the helmsman called out: “That was a whale! A big one swallows ships, and a small one can overturn a boat. Now luckily we did not meet it; I have been given a new life, a new life!” As night came on the wind and waves grew strong again, and the boat ran very fast. An Ui said: “I have heard that in the sea there is a dragon god, who is very greedy; let us throw some of our belongings in, to appease and thank him.” I did not respond. The people on the boat all said: “A man has this body, and only then does he have these things; these things are all things outside the body.” They vied to find such things as dyed clothing, weapons, iron implements and rations, and threw them into the sea. I too was unable to stop them.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初七日
paragraphs.en: 7th day

paragraphs.orig: 漂大洋中。是日陰，風勢甚惡，波浪洶湧。海色白。旌義縣監蔡允惠嘗謂臣曰，濟州父老云，天晴日登漢拏山絕頂，則遙望西南絕域，海外若有白沙汀一帶者，以今觀之，非白沙，乃望此白海而云也。臣謂權山等曰：「在高麗時，爾濟州朝大元，自明月浦，遇便風，得直路，七晝夜之間，過白海渡大洋。今我漂海，直路散路不可知也。幸得入白海之中，則竊疑中國之界必近矣。若得泊中國，則中國是我父母之邦也。當此時，生我死我，皆天所為。而風之順逆，天實主張。今東風不變已經累日，則抑竊疑天必有生我之心也。爾等其各勉人所當為之事，以聽天所命耳。」至暮，風又變東而北，權山猶指舵向西。夜未央，暴濤激躍，又駕入天篷，被人頭面，人皆瞑目不能開。領船、梢工皆痛哭，莫知所為。臣亦知不免於死，裂單衾纏身數圍，縛之於舟中橫木，蓋欲死後屍與舟久不相離也。莫金、巨伊山皆哭泣，聯抱臣身曰：「死且同歸！」安義大哭曰：「吾與其飲鹹水而死，莫如自絕！」以弓弦自縊。金粟救之，得不死。臣叫領船、梢工等曰：「舟已破乎？」曰：「否。」曰：「舵已失乎？」曰：「否。」即顧謂巨伊山曰：「波濤雖險，事勢雖迫，舟實牢固，不至易敗。若能汲殆盡，則庶幾得生。汝實壯健，汝又往首倡汲之。」巨伊山即命欲汲，汲水之器已盡破，叫號無據。安義即以刀裂去小鼓面以為器，授巨伊山。巨伊山與李孝枝、權松、都終、玄山等，盡力以汲水，猶深一膝，孝子、程保、李楨、金重等，或親自刮取，或立督軍人仇叱迴等七八人，相繼刮盡，僅得不見敗沒。
paragraphs.reading: 표대양중. 시일음, 풍세심악, 파랑흉용. 해색백. 정의현감채윤혜상위신왈, 제주부로운, 천청일등한라산절정, 칙요망서남절역, 해외약유백사정일대자, 이금관지, 비백사, 내망차백해이운야. 신위권산등왈: 「재고려시, 이제주조대원, 자명월포, 우편풍, 득직로, 칠주야지간, 과백해도대양. 금아표해, 직로산로불가지야. 행득입백해지중, 칙절의중국지계필근의. 약득박중국, 칙중국시아부모지방야. 당차시, 생아사아, 개천소위. 이풍지순역, 천실주장. 금동풍불변이경누일, 칙억절의천필유생아지심야. 이등기각면인소당위지사, 이청천소명이.」지모, 풍우변동이북, 권산유지타향서. 야미앙, 폭도격약, 우가입천봉, 피인두면, 인개명목불능개. 영선, 초공개통곡, 막지소위. 신역지불면어사, 열단금전신수위, 박지어주중횡목, 개욕사후시여주구불상리야. 막금, 거이산개곡읍, 연포신신왈: 「사차동귀!」안의대곡왈: 「오여기음함수이사, 막여자절!」이궁현자액. 김속구지, 득불사. 신규영선, 초공등왈: 「주이파호?」왈: 「부.」왈: 「타이실호?」왈: 「부.」즉고위거이산왈: 「파도수험, 사세수박, 주실뇌고, 부지이패. 약능급태진, 칙서기득생. 여실장건, 여우왕수창급지.」거이산즉명욕급, 급수지기이진파, 규호무거. 안의즉이도렬거소고면이위기, 수거이산. 거이산여이효지, 권송, 도종, 현산등, 진력이급수, 유심일슬, 효자, 정보, 이정, 김중등, 혹친자괄취, 혹입독군인구질회등칠팔인, 상계괄진, 근득불견패몰.
paragraphs.en: Drifting in the open ocean. That day overcast; the wind was fearsome and the waves surged. The colour of the sea was white. Chae Yunhye, Magistrate of Jeongui County, had once told me that the elders of Jeju say that on a clear day, if one climbs to the very summit of Mt. Hallasan and looks far to the south-west, beyond the remote borders it is as if there is a strip of white sandy shore beyond the sea; but now, looking back on it, I see it was not white sand — what they were speaking of, seen from afar, was this white sea. I said to Gwon San and the others: “In the Goryeo period, you people of Jeju went to court at the Great Yuan; setting out from Myeongwolpo, you caught a favourable wind, got a direct course, and in seven days and nights passed the White Sea and crossed the great ocean. Now that I am adrift on the sea, whether it is the direct route or a roundabout one cannot be known. If by luck we have entered the White Sea, then I privately suspect that the boundary of China must be near. If we can anchor in China, China is the land of our parents. At this time, whether it gives me life or death is all Heaven’s doing. And as to whether the wind is fair or foul, Heaven in truth rules it. Now the east wind has not changed for many days already, so I secretly suspect that Heaven must have a mind to let me live. You should each strive to do what men ought to do, and so await Heaven’s command.” At dusk the wind changed again from east to north, but Gwon San still pointed the rudder west. Before midnight a violent wave leapt up and again broke over the awning, covering people’s heads and faces; all shut their eyes and could not open them. The captain and the helmsman both wept bitterly and knew not what to do. I too knew that I would not escape death; I tore up a single quilt, wound it several times round my body, and bound myself to a transverse timber in the boat, intending that after death my corpse and the boat would not be parted for long. Makgeum and Geoisan both wept, and, clasping my body together, said: “Let us die and go back together!” An Ui cried out loudly: “Rather than drink salt water and die, better to kill myself!” and hanged himself with a bowstring. Kim Sok rescued him, and he did not die. I called to the captain and the helmsman: “Has the boat broken up?” “No.” “Has the rudder been lost?” “No.” Then I turned at once to Geoisan and said: “Though the waves are dangerous and the situation pressing, the boat is truly sturdy and will not easily be broken. If we can bail out almost all the water, there is hope of life. You are strong; go and lead the bailing again.” Geoisan at once set about bailing, but the vessels for bailing were all broken, and he shouted and cried out with nothing to rely on. An Ui at once tore the skin off a small drum with a knife to make a vessel and gave it to Geoisan. Geoisan, with Yi Hyoji, Gwon Song, Dojong, Hyeonsan and the others, bailed with all their strength; the water was still a knee deep, and Hyoja, Jeong Bo, Yi Jeong, Kim Jung and the others, some scooping with their own hands, some standing to direct the soldiers Gujilhoe and seven or eight others, scooped it all out in succession, and we barely escaped being wrecked and sunk.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初八日
paragraphs.en: 8th day

paragraphs.orig: 漂大洋中。是日陰，過午西北風又作。舟復退流向東南，徹夜而行。臣謂權山、高面、以福等曰：「汝等執舵正船，向方不可不知。我嘗閱地圖，自我國黑山島向東北行，即我忠清、黃海道界也；正北，即平安、遼東等處也；西北，即古《禹貢》青州、兗州之境也；正西，即徐州、揚州之域，宋時交通高麗，自明州浮海，明州即大江以南之地也；西南，即古閩地，今之福建路也；向西南，稍南而西，即暹羅、占城、滿剌加等國也；正南，即大小琉球國也；正南而東，即女人國也，一歧島也；正東，即日本國也，對馬州也。今漂風五晝夜，西向而來，意謂幾至中國之地。不幸又遭此西北風，逆向東南，若不至琉球國、女人國，則必流出天海之外，上達雲漢，無有涯涘。云如之何？汝等其記我言，正舵而去！」權山等曰：「天若開霽，測以日月星辰，猶未知海上四面。今則雲霧陰翳，日復一日，晨昏晝夜，俱不能記。衹以風之變作臆記四方耳。安知正方之可辨乎！」聚首而哭。
paragraphs.reading: 표대양중. 시일음, 과오서북풍우작. 주부퇴류향동남, 철야이행. 신위권산, 고면, 이복등왈: 「여등집타정선, 향방불가부지. 아상열지도, 자아국흑산도향동북행, 즉아충청, 황해도계야; 정북, 즉평안, 요동등처야; 서북, 즉고《우공》청주, 연주지경야; 정서, 즉서주, 양주지역, 송시교통고려, 자명주부해, 명주즉대강이남지지야; 서남, 즉고민지, 금지복건로야; 향서남, 초남이서, 즉섬라, 점성, 만랄가등국야; 정남, 즉대소유구국야; 정남이동, 즉여인국야, 일기도야; 정동, 즉일본국야, 대마주야. 금표풍오주야, 서향이래, 의위기지중국지지. 불행우조차서북풍, 역향동남, 약부지유구국, 여인국, 칙필유출천해지외, 상달운한, 무유애사. 운여지하? 여등기기아언, 정타이거!」권산등왈: 「천약개제, 측이일월성진, 유미지해상사면. 금칙운무음예, 일부일일, 신혼주야, 구불능기. 기이풍지변작억기사방이. 안지정방지가변호!」취수이곡.
paragraphs.en: Drifting in the open ocean. That day overcast; after noon the north-west wind arose again. The boat was again driven back towards the south-east and ran through the night. I said to Gwon San, Gomyeon, Ibok and the others: “You who hold the rudder and steady the ship must know the directions. I once looked at a map: going north-east from our Heuksan Island is the boundary of our Chungcheong and Hwanghae provinces; due north is Pyeongan, Liaodong and such places; north-west is the region of Qingzhou and Yanzhou of the ancient Yu Gong; due west is the domain of Xuzhou and Yangzhou — in the Song period, when communicating with Goryeo, they sailed from Mingzhou, and Mingzhou is the land south of the Great River; to the south-west is the ancient land of Min, today’s Fujian Circuit; going south-west, a little south of west, are Siam, Champa, Malacca and such countries; due south are the kingdoms of Great and Little Ryukyu; south and a little east is the Land of Women, and Iki Island; due east is the country of Japan, and Tsushima. Now, after drifting five days and nights, we came westward, and I thought we had almost reached the land of China. Unfortunately we have again met this north-west wind and been driven back towards the south-east; unless we reach the Ryukyu kingdom or the Land of Women, we shall surely flow out beyond the edge of heaven and sea, reaching up to the Milky Way, with no shore at all. What is to be done? Remember my words, and keep the rudder straight and go!” Gwon San and the others said: “Even if the sky were to clear and we measured by sun, moon and stars, we would still not know the four quarters of the sea. Now, with clouds and fog dark and overcast, day after day, morning and evening, day and night, we cannot even keep count. We merely guess the four directions from the changes in the wind. How should we know how to tell the true directions!” They put their heads together and wept.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初九日
paragraphs.en: 9th day

paragraphs.orig: 漂大洋中。是日片雲綴天。海色愈白。至是舟久為波濤所衝擊，梁頭、風梢、鼻隅三板皆動撓欲折，水又漏齧，將有自破之漸。斤寶、高面、尚理等截纜索，纏舟頭尾，削木補之。遂相向泣，且言曰：「若此修船，非不盡心，然飢渴將近旬矣。目無所見，手足痿痹，身不能保，力不能盡，故修之亦不能牢實，其將奈何？」倏有海鷗群飛而過。舟人望見喜曰：「嘗聞水鳥晝遊海上，夜宿島渚。我曹漂過滄溟萬里外，幸得見此鳥，則洲渚必不遠也。」臣曰：「鷗非一種，或浮沉江湖之渚者有之。若海鷗，則群在漲海中從潮飛翔，常以三月風至乃還洲嶼。今時則正月，鷗之群飛正在大海之中之時。」語未畢，又見有鸕鶿數雙飛去。臣亦稍疑島嶼之或近也。當午，南望雲氣作陣，依熹見山樣且有人煙之氣，意謂琉球國地界，將往泊。少選，東風又作，舟復向西。至夜，風勢愈緊，疾驅如飛。
paragraphs.reading: 표대양중. 시일편운철천. 해색유백. 지시주구위파도소충격, 양두, 풍초, 비우삼판개동요욕절, 수우루설, 장유자파지점. 근보, 고면, 상리등절람색, 전주두미, 삭목보지. 수상향읍, 차언왈: 「약차수선, 비부진심, 연기갈장근순의. 목무소견, 수족위비, 신불능보, 역불능진, 고수지역불능뇌실, 기장내하?」숙유해구군비이과. 주인망견희왈: 「상문수조주유해상, 야숙도저. 아조표과창명만리외, 행득견차조, 칙주저필불원야.」신왈: 「구비일종, 혹부침강호지저자유지. 약해구, 칙군재창해중종조비상, 상이삼월풍지내환주서. 금시칙정월, 구지군비정재대해지중지시.」어미필, 우견유로자수쌍비거. 신역초의도서지혹근야. 당오, 남망운기작진, 의희견산양차유인연지기, 의위유구국지계, 장왕박. 소선, 동풍우작, 주부향서. 지야, 풍세유긴, 질구여비.
paragraphs.en: Drifting in the open ocean. That day wisps of cloud dotted the sky. The colour of the sea was whiter still. By now the boat, long battered by the waves, had the three planks — the bow-beam, the wind-tail and the nose-corner — all shaking and twisting and about to snap, and water was also gnawing through; the boat was on the verge of breaking up of itself. Geunbo, Gomyeon, Sangni and the others cut cables and ropes and bound them round the bow and stern of the boat, and shaved wood to mend it. Then, facing each other, they wept and said: “In mending the boat like this, it is not that we have not put our hearts into it; but hunger and thirst have nearly reached ten days. Our eyes cannot see, our hands and feet are numb and paralysed, our bodies cannot protect themselves and our strength cannot do all that is needed; so even our mending cannot be firm and solid — what are we to do?” Suddenly a flock of sea gulls flew past. The people on the boat, seeing them, said gladly: “We have heard that water birds roam over the sea by day and roost on islands and sandbanks at night. We have drifted across the blue ocean for ten thousand li; if we are lucky enough to see these birds, then islets cannot be far.” I said: “Gulls are not of one kind; some float and sink on the shores of rivers and lakes. As for sea gulls, they gather in the swelling sea and fly with the tide, and always return to the islands when the wind comes in the third month. Now it is the first month, and gulls flying in flocks are precisely in the midst of the great sea.” Before I had finished speaking, we again saw a few pairs of cormorants fly by. I too began to suspect that islands might be near. At noon, looking south we saw the vapours of the clouds drawn up in ranks, faintly taking the shape of a mountain, with also the air of human habitation; I thought it was the border of the Ryukyu kingdom, and that we were about to go and anchor there. Shortly afterwards the east wind rose again, and the boat again headed west. By night the wind grew stronger still, and we were driven on swiftly as if flying.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初十日
paragraphs.en: 10th day

paragraphs.orig: 漂大洋中。是日雨，東風如昨。午後，海色還青。先是發濟州時，舟人無智，載陸水於鼻居舠以隨。自漂風後，相失莫值。所乘船中無一器甘水，未得漬炊，絕食絕飲，無可奈何。權松告於臣曰：「觀舟中人，或齎黃柑、清酒而來，恣食無餘。請括聚輸之上藏儲，以救渴可也。」臣即令巨伊山搜盡舟中行裝，得黃柑五十餘枚、酒二盆。謂孫孝子曰：「同舟則胡越一心，況我等皆一國人，情同骨肉，生則一時俱生，死則一時俱死。唯此柑酒，一滴千金。汝其掌之，毋得濫費，以救舟人一刻之渴可也。」孝子視人之唇焦口爛者，均分飲食之，止令沃舌。數日柑酒俱盡，或細嚼乾米，掬其溲溺以飲。未幾溲尿又竭，胸膈乾燥，不出聲氣，幾至死域。至是因雨下，舟人或以手擎篷榮聚其溜滴者；或以笠帽若鼎器貯其滲漉者；或屈席子奉其灑汛者；或建桅楫中約紙繩承其淋瀝者，期得些少一勺以舌舐之。安義曰：「濕雨以衣汁而取飲，所得誠多。但舟人之衣皆為鹹水所漬，雖濕雨而汁亦不能飲，若之何其？」臣即點出所藏衣數領，令巨伊山承雨露洽，取汁以貯，幾至數瓶。令金重用匙分飲之。重執匙以舉，舟人張口，有如燕兒望哺然。自是始能掉舌噓氣，稍有向生之心。
paragraphs.reading: 표대양중. 시일우, 동풍여작. 오후, 해색환청. 선시발제주시, 주인무지, 재육수어비거도이수. 자표풍후, 상실막치. 소승선중무일기감수, 미득지취, 절식절음, 무가내하. 권송고어신왈: 「관주중인, 혹재황감, 청주이래, 자식무여. 청괄취수지상장저, 이구갈가야.」신즉영거이산수진주중행장, 득황감오십여매, 주이분. 위손효자왈: 「동주칙호월일심, 황아등개일국인, 정동골육, 생칙일시구생, 사칙일시구사. 유차감주, 일적천금. 여기장지, 무득남비, 이구주인일각지갈가야.」효자시인지진초구란자, 균분음식지, 지영옥설. 수일감주구진, 혹세작건미, 국기수닉이음. 미기수뇨우갈, 흉격건조, 불출성기, 기지사역. 지시인우하, 주인혹이수경봉영취기류적자; 혹이입모약정기저기삼록자; 혹굴석자봉기쇄신자; 혹건외즙중약지승승기임력자, 기득사소일작이설지지. 안의왈: 「습우이의즙이취음, 소득성다. 단주인지의개위함수소지, 수습우이즙역불능음, 약지하기?」신즉점출소장의수령, 영거이산승우로흡, 취즙이저, 기지수병. 영김중용시분음지. 중집시이거, 주인장구, 유여연아망포연. 자시시능도설허기, 초유향생지심.
paragraphs.en: Drifting in the open ocean. That day rain, and the east wind as the day before. After noon the colour of the sea turned blue again. Earlier, when we left Jeju, the men of the boat, being unwise, had loaded fresh water from land into a tender (bigeoju) to follow us. After we were blown away by the storm, we lost each other and never met again. In the boat we rode there was not a single vessel of sweet water, and we could not soak rice for cooking; without food or drink, nothing could be done. Gwon Song said to me: “Looking at the men in the boat, some have brought yellow tangerines and clear wine and eat them freely until none is left. Please collect them all and hand them over to be stored aloft, and use them to relieve thirst.” I at once had Geoisan search all the baggage in the boat and got fifty-odd yellow tangerines and two jars of wine. I said to Son Hyoja: “In the same boat even men of Hu and Yue are of one mind; how much more are we all people of one country, our feelings like those of flesh and blood. If we live, we all live together; if we die, we all die together. This fruit and wine alone is worth a thousand in gold per drop. You take charge of it, and do not squander it; use it to relieve the thirst of the men in the boat for a moment.” Hyoja, seeing people with scorched lips and ulcerated mouths, divided the food and drink among them equally, only letting them moisten their tongues. After a few days the tangerines and wine were both gone, and some chewed dry rice finely, or cupped their own urine in their hands and drank it. Before long the urine too ran dry; chests and diaphragms were parched, they could make no voice or breath, and were almost in the realm of death. By now, because rain fell, the men of the boat held up their hands to catch the drips from the edge of the awning; or used straw hats and caps, cauldrons and vessels to store what seeped through; or bent mats to receive what spattered; or set up the mast and oars and tied paper cords in the middle to receive the dripping — hoping to get a small spoonful, and licked it up with the tongue. An Ui said: “Wetting clothes in the rain and squeezing out the juice to drink would yield a great deal. But the clothes of the men on the boat are all soaked with salt water; even if wetted by the rain, the juice cannot be drunk; what can we do?” I at once brought out several garments I had stored and had Geoisan expose them to the rain until thoroughly wet, and take the liquid and store it, almost several bottles. I had Kim Jung give it out to drink with a spoon. Jung held the spoon and lifted it, and the men of the boat opened their mouths like swallow chicks looking for food. From this time they could at last move their tongues and breathe out, and gradually had a mind toward life.

paragraphs.orig: ## △十一日
paragraphs.en: 11th day

paragraphs.orig: 漂大洋中。是日陰。清晨至一島，石壁嵯峨，甚險峨。海波震蕩，激上磊礐，幾一二丈，舟隨波直入，勢迫擊碎。權山大哭，遂竭力運船。孝子、程保等亦親攬帆邊阿綯，視風波，或縱或引。時則水從海入島，風從島出海，舟從風回旋，得免於患。夕，至一大島，島又岩石削立，欲泊舟不得。以福脫衣躍入水中，拽舟遊泳，緣島岸以繫。舟人喜倒闌，下覓溪流，抔甘水而飲，負汲欲做飯。臣曰：「飢餓之極，五臟塗附，若驟得食飽則必死！莫若先飲漿水，繼之以粥，適可而止可也。」舟人皆煎粥而啜。島無避風處，故夜又縱舟而去。
paragraphs.reading: 표대양중. 시일음. 청신지일도, 석벽차아, 심험아. 해파진탕, 격상뇌확, 기일이장, 주수파직입, 세박격쇄. 권산대곡, 수갈력운선. 효자, 정보등역친람범변아도, 시풍파, 혹종혹인. 시칙수종해입도, 풍종도출해, 주종풍회선, 득면어환. 석, 지일대도, 도우암석삭립, 욕박주부득. 이복탈의약입수중, 예주유영, 연도안이계. 주인희도란, 하멱계류, 부감수이음, 부급욕주반. 신왈: 「기아지극, 오장도부, 약취득식포칙필사! 막약선음장수, 계지이죽, 적가이지가야.」주인개전죽이철. 도무피풍처, 고야우종주이거.
paragraphs.en: Drifting in the open ocean. That day overcast. At dawn we reached an island whose rock cliffs towered, extremely precipitous. The sea waves shook and surged, dashing against the boulders one or two zhang high, and the boat, riding the waves, went straight in; the situation pressed us to the verge of being smashed. Gwon San wept loudly and then with all his strength handled the boat. Hyoja, Jeong Bo and the others also themselves gripped the sail ropes at the edge of the sail, watching the wind and waves, letting out or hauling in. At that time the water flowed from the sea into the island, the wind blew from the island out to sea, and the boat turned about with the wind, and so we escaped the disaster. In the evening we reached a large island, whose rock faces were again sheer, and we could not moor. Ibok took off his clothes and leapt into the water, swam towing the boat, and secured it along the shore. The men of the boat were delighted beyond measure; they went down to look for a stream and cupped sweet water in their hands to drink, and carried water on their backs to cook rice. I said: “In extreme hunger the five viscera cling together; if you suddenly get food and eat your fill, you will surely die! It is better first to drink thin rice-water, then follow with gruel, and stop at the right moment.” The men of the boat all boiled gruel and sipped it. The island had no place sheltered from the wind, so at night we again let the boat go and went on.

paragraphs.orig: ## △十二日
paragraphs.en: 12th day

paragraphs.orig: 遇賊於寧波府界。是日乍陰乍雨。海色還白。晡，至巨島，連綿如屏。望有中船二艘，皆帶懸居舠，直指臣船而來。程保等羅跪臣前曰：「凡事有經有權，請解喪服，權著紗帽、團領，以示官人之儀。不然，則彼必哄我為劫賊，加以僇辱矣。」臣曰：「漂流海上，天也；屢經死地而復生，天也；到此島而遇此船，亦天也。天理本直，安可違天以行詐乎？」俄頃，二船漸近相值。一船可十餘人，人皆穿黑襺褲、芒鞋，有以手帕裹頭者，有著竹葉笠、棕皮蓑者，喧豗叫噪，渾是漢語。臣度其乃是中國人。令程保書紙以遺曰：「朝鮮國臣崔溥，奉王命往海島。奔父喪，過海遇風，漂到不知是何國邑地也。」其人復曰：「此乃大唐國浙江寧波府地方。」又曰：「要到本國去，須到大唐好。」程保以手指其口。其人以陸水二桶來遺，棹舟東去。臣令舟人櫓入一島以依。
paragraphs.reading: 우적어영파부계. 시일사음사우. 해색환백. 포, 지거도, 연면여병. 망유중선이소, 개대현거도, 직지신선이래. 정보등나궤신전왈: 「범사유경유권, 청해상복, 권착사모, 단령, 이시관인지의. 불연, 칙피필홍아위겁적, 가이육욕의.」신왈: 「표류해상, 천야; 누경사지이부생, 천야; 도차도이우차선, 역천야. 천리본직, 안가위천이행사호?」아경, 이선점근상치. 일선가십여인, 인개천흑견고, 망혜, 유이수말과두자, 유착죽엽립, 종피사자, 훤회규조, 혼시한어. 신탁기내시중국인. 영정보서지이유왈: 「조선국신최부, 봉왕명왕해도. 분부상, 과해우풍, 표도부지시하국읍지야.」기인부왈: 「차내대당국절강영파부지방.」우왈: 「요도본국거, 수도대당호.」정보이수지기구. 기인이육수이통래유, 도주동거. 신영주인로입일도이의.
paragraphs.en: Encountered pirates in the territory of Ningbo Prefecture. That day alternately overcast and rainy. The colour of the sea was white again. In the late afternoon we reached a large island, continuous like a screen. We saw two medium-sized vessels, each towing a “hanging-dwelling” tender (xuanjudao), coming straight toward our boat. Jeong Bo and the others knelt in a row before me and said: “In all things there is the constant and the expedient. Please take off the mourning garb and, as an expedient, put on a gauze cap and round-collared robe to show the bearing of a government official. Otherwise they will surely take us for robbers and add humiliation and slaughter.” I said: “That we drifted on the sea was Heaven; that we repeatedly passed through places of death and lived again was Heaven; that we came to this island and met these boats is also Heaven. The principle of Heaven is straight at root — how can we go against Heaven and practise deceit?” Shortly the two boats gradually drew near and met us. In one boat were about ten or more men, all wearing black quilted trousers and straw sandals; some had cloths wrapped round their heads, and some wore bamboo-leaf hats and palm-bark rain-capes; they were shouting and clamouring, all in Chinese. I judged that they were Chinese. I had Jeong Bo write on paper and send it over: “I am Choe Bu, a subject of the Kingdom of Joseon, sent by royal command to an island in the sea. Hastening to my father’s funeral I crossed the sea and met a storm, and have drifted here, I know not to what country’s land.” The man replied: “This is the Great Tang country, the district of Ningbo Prefecture in Zhejiang.” And he added: “If you want to go to your own country, it is good to go to the Great Tang.” Jeong Bo pointed with his hand to his mouth. The man sent over two buckets of fresh water from land, and rowed his boat away to the east. I ordered the men of the boat to scull into an island and moor by it.

paragraphs.orig: 又有一艘亦帶懸居舠，有軍人可七八人——其衣服語音亦與前所見同，——來逆臣船，曰：「你是何國人？」臣又使程保答如前。因問曰：「此何國地？」其人指其島曰：「此即大唐寧波府地下山也。風水好，二日可回去。」臣又復曰：「他國人遭風，萬死之餘，幸到大國之境，喜得復生之地！」又問渠姓名謂誰？其人答曰：「我是大唐林大。你若大唐去，帶你進去。你有寶貨可遺我？」臣答曰：「僕奉使臣非商賈者流，且漂流浮沉之後，安有寶貨乎？」即減米糧以饋之。其人受而復曰：「此山繫船不怕西北風，但南風不好，隨我繫船！」引臣船，指一泊舟島曰：「此可泊，可泊！」臣如其言，即往泊之，果無風，環島中可藏船處也。其西岸有二草屋，如鮑作幹家者，其人等泊於屋下。臣之同舟人，久饑久渴久勞久不寢寐之極，得食以食，得風定處以泊，困憊支羸，相與枕藉乎舟中。
paragraphs.reading: 우유일소역대현거도, 유군인가칠팔인——기의복어음역여전소견동, ——내역신선, 왈: 「이시하국인?」신우사정보답여전. 인문왈: 「차하국지?」기인지기도왈: 「차즉대당영파부지하산야. 풍수호, 이일가회거.」신우부왈: 「타국인조풍, 만사지여, 행도대국지경, 희득부생지지!」우문거성명위수? 기인답왈: 「아시대당임대. 이약대당거, 대이진거. 이유보화가유아?」신답왈: 「복봉사신비상고자류, 차표류부침지후, 안유보화호?」즉감미량이궤지. 기인수이부왈: 「차산계선불파서북풍, 단남풍불호, 수아계선!」인신선, 지일박주도왈: 「차가박, 가박!」신여기언, 즉왕박지, 과무풍, 환도중가장선처야. 기서안유이초옥, 여포작간가자, 기인등박어옥하. 신지동주인, 구기구갈구로구불침매지극, 득식이식, 득풍정처이박, 곤비지리, 상여침자호주중.
paragraphs.en: There was another vessel, also towing a hanging-dwelling tender, with some seven or eight soldiers — their clothing and speech also the same as those seen before — who came to meet my boat and said: “What country are you from?” I again had Jeong Bo answer as before. Then I asked: “What country is this land?” The man pointed to the island and said: “This is Xiashan, in Ningbo Prefecture of the Great Tang. The wind and water are good; you could return in two days.” I again said: “We people of another country met a storm, and after ten thousand deaths have happily reached the border of the great country; it is a place of joy, where we recover life!” I also asked his name. The man answered: “I am Lin Da of the Great Tang. If you go to the Great Tang, I will take you in. Do you have any treasure to give me?” I answered: “I am an envoy, not of the class of merchants, and after drifting and sinking, how should I have treasure?” I at once spared some of our rice and provisions to give to him. The man took it and said again: “At this mountain, boats moored need not fear the north-west wind, but the south wind is not good. Follow me and moor.” He led my boat, and pointing to a mooring island said: “Here you can moor, you can moor!” I did as he said and went to moor there; indeed there was no wind: it was a place within the encircling island where boats could be hidden. On its west shore were two grass huts, like the houses of those who dry abalone, and these men moored below the huts. My fellow-boatmen, at the extreme of long hunger, long thirst, long toil and long sleeplessness, having eaten what food they could get, having moored where the wind was still, exhausted and weak, lay down together in heaps in the boat.

paragraphs.orig: 夜二更，所謂自稱林大者，率其黨二十餘人，或執槍或帶斫刀——而無弓箭——秉炬擁至，闖入臣船。賊魁書曰：「我是觀音佛，洞見你心。你有金銀便覓看！」臣答曰：「金銀非本國所產，初無有齎。」賊魁曰：「你若官人豈不齎來？我當看看。」初，臣及程保、李楨、金重、孝子等，以濟州海外地，往來無期，具四節衣服數套而往。至是賊魁即叫其黨，窮搜臣及陪吏等包中衣裝、舟人糧物，輸載其船。其所遺名，若衣之濃沾鹹水者及諸般書冊而已。賊中眇一目者，惡之尤甚。程保謂臣曰：「賊之始至，示若從容，見我勢弱，馴成大賊。請—奮擊，以決死生！」臣曰：「我舟人皆以饑渴垂死之後奪氣於賊，故賊乘勢肆暴，若與相搏，則我輩皆死於賊手，莫如盡付行李以乞生活耳。」賊魁又奪臣所齎印信、馬牌，納之懷袖。程保尾其後請還不得。臣曰：「船中有物可盡取去。印與馬牌乃國之信，私無可用，可還我。」賊魁以印、牌還。才出篷窗，與其黨列立船舷，喧囂良久，旋入船中。先脫程保衣褲，捆而杖之。次以斫刀截臣衣紐，赤身剝脫，背手曲腳以綁之，以杖杖臣左臂七八下，曰：「你若愛生，便出金銀！」臣大號曰：「身可臠，骨可碎，何所得金銀乎？」賊不曉臣言，解臣縛，許以寫意。臣即寫之。賊魁怒，嗔目張喙，指程保而叫，指臣而叫，即曳臣頭髮，還縛倒懸，荷斫刀指臣頸斫之，刀適誤下右肩隅，刃翻在上，賊又荷刀將斬臣，有一賊來把荷刀之臂以沮之。賊黨齊聲大叫，莫知所謂。是時，舟人惴懼失常，奔竄無地，唯金重、巨伊山等攢手拜跪，冀活臣命。俄而，賊魁蹂躪臣身，喝嚇舟人，引其黨而出。截去臣船碇櫓諸椽，投諸海，遂以其船導牽臣船，指放大洋，然後乘其船遁去。夜已闌矣。
paragraphs.reading: 야이경, 소위자칭임대자, 솔기당이십여인, 혹집창혹대작도——이무궁전——병거옹지, 틈입신선. 적괴서왈: 「아시관음불, 통견이심. 이유금은편멱간!」신답왈: 「금은비본국소산, 초무유재.」적괴왈: 「이약관인기부재래? 아당간간.」초, 신급정보, 이정, 김중, 효자등, 이제주해외지, 왕래무기, 구사절의복수투이왕. 지시적괴즉규기당, 궁수신급배리등포중의장, 주인량물, 수재기선. 기소유명, 약의지농첨함수자급제반서책이이. 적중묘일목자, 악지우심. 정보위신왈: 「적지시지, 시약종용, 견아세약, 순성대적. 청—분격, 이결사생!」신왈: 「아주인개이기갈수사지후탈기어적, 고적승세사포, 약여상박, 칙아배개사어적수, 막여진부행리이걸생활이.」적괴우탈신소재인신, 마패, 납지회수. 정보미기후청환부득. 신왈: 「선중유물가진취거. 인여마패내국지신, 사무가용, 가환아.」적괴이인, 패환. 재출봉창, 여기당열립선현, 훤효양구, 선입선중. 선탈정보의고, 곤이장지. 차이작도절신의뉴, 적신박탈, 배수곡각이방지, 이장장신좌비칠팔하, 왈: 「이약애생, 편출금은!」신대호왈: 「신가련, 골가쇄, 하소득금은호?」적불효신언, 해신박, 허이사의. 신즉사지. 적괴로, 진목장훼, 지정보이규, 지신이규, 즉예신두발, 환박도현, 하작도지신경작지, 도적오하우견우, 인번재상, 적우하도장참신, 유일적래파하도지비이저지. 적당제성대규, 막지소위. 시시, 주인췌구실상, 분찬무지, 유김중, 거이산등찬수배궤, 기활신명. 아이, 적괴유린신신, 갈하주인, 인기당이출. 절거신선정로제연, 투제해, 수이기선도견신선, 지방대양, 연후승기선둔거. 야이란의.
paragraphs.en: At the second watch of the night, the one who had called himself Lin Da, leading his gang of twenty or more, some holding spears and some carrying cutlasses — but without bows and arrows — came crowding with torches and burst into my boat. The chief of the robbers wrote: “I am the Buddha Guanyin; I see right into your heart. If you have gold and silver, bring it out and let me see!” I answered: “Gold and silver are not products of our country, and I never brought any.” The chief said: “If you are an official, how could you not have brought it? I shall look.” At the outset, because Jeju was an overseas place with no fixed time of going and returning, I, Jeong Bo, Yi Jeong, Kim Jung, Hyoja and the others had gone bringing several sets of clothing for the four seasons. At this, the chief at once called to his gang and searched thoroughly through the bundles of clothing of me and my attendant clerks and the boatmen’s grain and goods, and loaded them into their boat. What they left behind, as it were, was only clothing thickly soaked with salt water and assorted books. Among the robbers there was a one-eyed man who was especially vicious. Jeong Bo said to me: “When the robbers first arrived, they pretended to be at ease; seeing our weakness, they gradually became great robbers. Please let us strike with all our might and decide life and death!” I said: “The men of my boat have all, after being near death from hunger and thirst, had their spirit snatched away by the robbers, so the robbers take advantage and are violent. If we fight them, we shall all die at the robbers’ hands; better to hand over all our baggage and beg for our lives.” The chief further seized the seal and horse-tablet I had brought and put them in his sleeve. Jeong Bo followed behind and asked for them back but could not get them. I said: “Everything in the boat you may take. The seal and horse-tablet are the credentials of the state and are of no use to you privately; give them back to me.” The chief returned the seal and tablet. As soon as he went out of the awning window, he stood with his gang on the gunwale, clamouring for a long time, then came back into the boat. First he stripped off Jeong Bo’s clothes and trousers, trussed him and beat him with a stick. Next he cut the cords of my clothes with his cutlass, stripped me naked, tied my hands behind my back with my legs bent, and bound me, and with a stick struck my left arm seven or eight times, saying: “If you love life, then bring out your gold and silver!” I cried out loudly: “My body may be minced, my bones may be shattered — where would I get gold and silver?” The robber did not understand my words, untied my bonds and allowed me to write what I meant. I wrote it at once. The chief was enraged; glaring and gaping, he pointed at Jeong Bo and shouted, pointed at me and shouted, and seized my hair and dragged me, bound me again hanging upside down, shouldered his cutlass and cut at my neck; the blade happened to miss and fall on the corner of my right shoulder, the edge turning upward; the robber again shouldered the blade, about to behead me, when one robber came and grasped the arm that carried the blade to hinder him. The robbers cried out together, and I knew not what they said. At that time the boatmen, terrified, lost their composure and scattered with nowhere to run; only Kim Jung, Geoisan and the others clasped their hands and knelt and bowed, hoping to save my life. Presently the chief trampled on my body, bellowed at the boatmen, and led his gang out. They cut away our boat’s anchor, sculls and rafters, throwing them into the sea, and then with their own boat towed my boat and, pointing us out to the open ocean, afterward left in their boat and fled. The night was already far gone.

paragraphs.orig: ## △十三日
paragraphs.en: 13th day

paragraphs.orig: 復漂大洋中。是日陰。西北風大起，又流入無涯之海。臣及舟人所藏襺衣俱失於賊。所穿之衣久漬鹹水，天且恒陰，不得曝乾，凍死之期逼矣；舟載儲糧盡為賊奪，餓死之期逼矣；舟以碇櫓為賊所投，假帆為風所破，但隨風東西，隨潮出入，梢工無所施其力，沉沒之期亦逼矣。舟人皆填噎，莫能出聲，坐待死期。孝枝謂臣曰：「我等之死，分內事也，衹以敬差官之死為痛惜耳。」臣曰：「爾何以死地為分內乎？」孝枝曰：「我州邈在大海中，水路九百餘里，波濤視諸海尤為洶暴。貢船商舶絡繹不絕，漂沒沉溺十居五六。州人不死於前，則必死於後。故境中男墳最少，閭閻之間，女多三倍於男。為父母者，生女則必曰是善孝我者；生男則皆曰此物非我兒，乃鯨鼉之食也。我等之死如蜉蝣出沒，雖在平日亦豈以死於牖下為心哉？唯朝臣往來，從容待風，舟楫儇牢，故死於風波者前古所罕。適于今敬差官之身天不陰佑，至於不測之地，是以痛哭耳。」
paragraphs.reading: 부표대양중. 시일음. 서북풍대기, 우유입무애지해. 신급주인소장견의구실어적. 소천지의구지함수, 천차항음, 부득폭건, 동사지기핍의; 주재저량진위적탈, 아사지기핍의; 주이정로위적소투, 가범위풍소파, 단수풍동서, 수조출입, 초공무소시기력, 침몰지기역핍의. 주인개전열, 막능출성, 좌대사기. 효지위신왈: 「아등지사, 분내사야, 기이경차관지사위통석이.」신왈: 「이하이사지위분내호?」효지왈: 「아주막재대해중, 수로구백여리, 파도시제해우위흉포. 공선상박낙역부절, 표몰침닉십거오륙. 주인불사어전, 칙필사어후. 고경중남분최소, 여염지간, 여다삼배어남. 위부모자, 생녀칙필왈시선효아자; 생남칙개왈차물비아아, 내경타지식야. 아등지사여부유출몰, 수재평일역기이사어유하위심재? 유조신왕래, 종용대풍, 주즙현뢰, 고사어풍파자전고소한. 적우금경차관지신천불음우, 지어불측지지, 시이통곡이.」
paragraphs.en: Again drifting in the open ocean. That day overcast. A strong north-west wind arose, and again we flowed into the boundless sea. The quilted clothes that I and the boatmen had stored were all lost to the robbers. The clothes we wore had long been soaked in salt water, and the sky was constantly overcast, so they could not be dried in the sun; the time to freeze to death was pressing. The provisions stored in the boat were all seized by the robbers; the time to starve to death was pressing. The boat’s anchor and sculls had been thrown away by the robbers, and the makeshift sail had been broken by the wind; we could only go east and west with the wind and in and out with the tide, the helmsman had no way to use his strength, and the time of sinking was also pressing. The men of the boat were all choked with grief and could not utter a sound, sitting to await the day of death. Hyoji said to me: “Our deaths are within our lot; we only grieve for the death of the Special Commissioner.” I said: “Why do you regard places of death as within your lot?” Hyoji said: “Our province lies far in the great sea, nine hundred li or so by water, and its waves are more violent than those of any other sea. Tribute ships and merchant vessels come one after another without ceasing, and five or six out of ten are wrecked and drowned. If the people of the province do not die earlier, then they die later. So in our territory men’s graves are fewest, and in the villages women outnumber men three to one. Parents who bear a girl always say, ‘This one will be good to us’; those who bear a boy all say, ‘This is not my child, it is food for whales and sea-monsters.’ Our deaths are like those of mayflies, rising and vanishing; even in ordinary times, do we have in mind to die under the window at home? Only for court officials who come and go, calmly waiting for the wind, with boats and oars light and sturdy, deaths from storm and wave were rare in former times. And now to the Special Commissioner Heaven gives no secret aid, bringing him to an unfathomable place, and so we weep bitterly.”

paragraphs.orig: ## △十四日
paragraphs.en: 14th day

paragraphs.orig: 漂大洋中。是日睛。晡時，漂至一島，東西南三面，一望無際，唯可避北風處。顧以無碇為憂。初發濟州時，舟甚大，無載物，故輸若干石塊於舟中，使不能撓動。至是尚理等以絞索纏其石，四個合為假碇，以留泊焉。安義與軍人等相與言，使之聞之於臣曰：「此行所以至於漂死者，我知之矣。自古以來，凡往濟州者，皆祭於光州無等山祠及羅州錦城山祠；自濟州出陸者，又皆祭於廣壤、遮歸、川外、楚春等祠，然後行，故受神之祐，利涉大海。今此敬差官特大言非之，來不祭無等、錦城之祠，去不祭廣壤諸祠。慢神不敬，神亦不恤，使至此極，尚誰咎哉？」軍人和之，咸咎臣。權松獨曰：「不然。前此李旌義暹，三日致齋，精祀廣壤等神，亦至漂流，幾死復延。權敬差官景祜俱不致祭，尚且往來快順，亡些子恙。則過海便否，在於待風之如何耳，豈關於神之祭不祭哉？」臣亦誨之曰：「天地無私，鬼神默運，福善禍淫，唯其公耳。人有惡者，諂事以徼福，則其可福之乎？人有善者，不惑邪說，不為黷祭，則其可禍之乎？曾謂天地鬼神為諂事飲食，而降禍福於人乎？萬萬無此理也。況祭有常等，士庶人而祭山川非禮也。非禮之祭乃淫祀也。淫祀以獲福者，我未之見也。爾濟州人酷好鬼神，山澤川藪俱設神祠，至如廣壤等堂，朝夕敬祀，靡所不至。其於涉海，宜無漂沉之患，然而今日某船漂，明日某船沉，漂沉之船前後相望，是果神有靈應歟？祭能受福歟？況今我同舟人，不祭者唯我一人耳，爾軍人皆誠心齋祭而來，神若有靈，豈以我一人不祭之故廢爾四十餘人齋祭之誠也？我之漂船，專是行李顛倒，不善候風之所致，反以廢祭尤我，不亦惑乎！」安義等猶以臣言為迂闊，不以為是。
paragraphs.reading: 표대양중. 시일정. 포시, 표지일도, 동서남삼면, 일망무제, 유가피북풍처. 고이무정위우. 초발제주시, 주심대, 무재물, 고수약간석괴어주중, 사불능요동. 지시상리등이교색전기석, 사개합위가정, 이류박언. 안의여군인등상여언, 사지문지어신왈: 「차행소이지어표사자, 아지지의. 자고이래, 범왕제주자, 개제어광주무등산사급나주금성산사; 자제주출륙자, 우개제어광양, 차귀, 천외, 초춘등사, 연후행, 고수신지우, 이섭대해. 금차경차관특대언비지, 내부제무등, 금성지사, 거부제광양제사. 만신불경, 신역불휼, 사지차극, 상수구재?」군인화지, 함구신. 권송독왈: 「불연. 전차이정의섬, 삼일치재, 정사광양등신, 역지표류, 기사부연. 권경차관경호구불치제, 상차왕래쾌순, 망사자양. 칙과해편부, 재어대풍지여하이, 기관어신지제부제재?」신역회지왈: 「천지무사, 귀신묵운, 복선화음, 유기공이. 인유악자, 첨사이요복, 칙기가복지호? 인유선자, 불혹사설, 불위독제, 칙기가화지호? 증위천지귀신위첨사음식, 이강화복어인호? 만만무차리야. 황제유상등, 사서인이제산천비례야. 비례지제내음사야. 음사이획복자, 아미지견야. 이제주인혹호귀신, 산택천수구설신사, 지여광양등당, 조석경사, 미소부지. 기어섭해, 의무표침지환, 연이금일모선표, 명일모선침, 표침지선전후상망, 시과신유령응여? 제능수복여? 황금아동주인, 부제자유아일인이, 이군인개성심재제이래, 신약유령, 기이아일인부제지고폐이사십여인재제지성야? 아지표선, 전시행리전도, 불선후풍지소치, 반이폐제우아, 불역혹호!」안의등유이신언위우활, 불이위시.
paragraphs.en: Drifting in the open ocean. That day fair. In the late afternoon we drifted to an island whose east, west and south sides were open to the view without limit, with only one place that could shelter from the north wind. We worried only that we had no anchor. When we first left Jeju the boat was very large and carried no cargo, so a number of stones had been loaded into the boat to keep it from shaking. Now Sangni and the others bound the stones with twisted ropes, four together to make a makeshift anchor, and so we moored. An Ui and the soldiers talked together and had me hear it, saying: “I know why this trip has come to drifting and death. From antiquity, all who go to Jeju sacrifice at the shrine of Mt. Mudeung in Gwangju and the shrine of Mt. Geumseong in Naju; and those who leave Jeju for the mainland also sacrifice at the shrines of Gwangyang, Chagwi, Cheonoe, Chochun and others, and then go; so they receive the spirits’ help and cross the great sea safely. This time the Special Commissioner made a great show of denying it, and on the way coming he did not sacrifice at the shrines of Mudeung and Geumseong, nor on the way going at Gwangyang and the other shrines. Being disrespectful to the spirits, the spirits too do not take pity on us, and have brought us to this extreme — whom else can we blame?” The soldiers echoed him and all blamed me. Gwon Song alone said: “Not so. Before this, Yi Seom, the Jeongui magistrate, fasted three days and sacrificed devoutly to the spirits of Gwangyang and others, and yet he drifted and nearly died before his life was spared. The Special Commissioner Gwon Gyeongho sacrificed to none of them, and yet his coming and going was fast and smooth, without the slightest harm. So whether the crossing goes well or not depends on how one waits for the wind; what has it to do with whether sacrifices are made to the spirits?” I too instructed them: “Heaven and Earth have no partiality; the spirits work in silence; they bless the good and bring misfortune on the licentious, solely out of fairness. If a wicked man flatters the spirits to seek blessing, can they bless him? If a good man is not deceived by heterodox teaching and does not defile himself with excessive sacrifices, can they bring him misfortune? Did you ever suppose that Heaven, Earth and the spirits are flattered by food and drink and send down weal and woe on people? There is no such principle at all. Moreover, sacrifice has regular grades: for gentlemen and commoners to sacrifice to mountains and rivers is contrary to ritual. A sacrifice contrary to ritual is a lewd cult. I have never seen anyone obtain blessings through lewd cults. You people of Jeju are inordinately fond of spirits, and have set up shrines to spirits in mountains, marshes, rivers and thickets, and as for halls such as Gwangyang, you sacrifice there morning and evening with the utmost reverence. By rights there should be no danger of drifting or sinking in your sea-crossings; and yet today such-and-such a boat drifts and tomorrow such-and-such a boat sinks; drifted and sunken boats follow in sight of one another — is it truly that the spirits are efficacious? That sacrifices can bring blessing? Moreover, among those on this boat, the only one who did not sacrifice is I alone; you soldiers all came having fasted and sacrificed with sincere hearts. If the spirits are efficacious, how would they, because of the one man who did not sacrifice, set aside the sincerity of the fast and sacrifice of you forty or more? That my boat drifted was due entirely to the baggage being tumbled about and to not knowing how to wait well for the wind; to blame me in return for omitting the sacrifice — is that not deluded?” An Ui and the others still thought my words impractical and did not accept them as right.

paragraphs.orig: ## △十五日
paragraphs.en: 15th day

paragraphs.orig: 漂大洋中。是日陰。海色赤而濁。東風復起又順風指舵於西。舟中人，若朴終回、萬山、李山等，有疾病不堪事；高保終、梁達海、高回、金朝回、任山海等，自漂海以至是日，臥不起動，雖督之以取露等事，聽之藐藐；鄭實、夫命同、金得時、姜有、宋真、金粟、姜內、吳山、高內乙同等，十喚一應，或有不得已而從事者；肖斤寶、金怪山、高福、金松、金石貴、李孝台、金真山等，或晝勤夜怠，或始勤終怠；許尚理、權山、金高面、金仇叱回、崔巨伊山、金都終、高以福、文回、玄山、韓每山、權松、莫金等，晝夜不怠，以運船為己任；程保、金重、李楨、孫孝子、李孝枝、安義等，或親自服役或檢督治船，以期完事。自遇賊復漂以後，人皆無意於生，漸不如前。舟為暴濤所擊，為日已久，百孔千瘡，旋塞旋缺，罅漏有水，將不勝汲。臣曰：「漏水若此，舟人之解體又若此，我其妄自尊大，坐見溺死，胡可哉？」遂與程保等六人親自刮水幾盡。尚理以下十餘人亦稍有奮力而起者。夜，無風而雨，至一大島，為汐勢所逆依泊不得，中流海上。
paragraphs.reading: 표대양중. 시일음. 해색적이탁. 동풍부기우순풍지타어서. 주중인, 약박종회, 만산, 이산등, 유질병불감사; 고보종, 양달해, 고회, 김조회, 임산해등, 자표해이지시일, 와불기동, 수독지이취로등사, 청지묘묘; 정실, 부명동, 김득시, 강유, 송진, 김속, 강내, 오산, 고내을동등, 십환일응, 혹유부득이이종사자; 초근보, 김괴산, 고복, 김송, 김석귀, 이효태, 김진산등, 혹주근야태, 혹시근종태; 허상리, 권산, 김고면, 김구질회, 최거이산, 김도종, 고이복, 문회, 현산, 한매산, 권송, 막금등, 주야불태, 이운선위기임; 정보, 김중, 이정, 손효자, 이효지, 안의등, 혹친자복역혹검독치선, 이기완사. 자우적부표이후, 인개무의어생, 점불여전. 주위폭도소격, 위일이구, 백공천창, 선색선결, 하루유수, 장불승급. 신왈: 「누수약차, 주인지해체우약차, 아기망자존대, 좌견익사, 호가재?」수여정보등육인친자괄수기진. 상리이하십여인역초유분력이기자. 야, 무풍이우, 지일대도, 위석세소역의박부득, 중류해상.
paragraphs.en: Drifting in the open ocean. That day overcast. The colour of the sea was red and turbid. An east wind rose again, and again with a following wind we aimed the rudder west. Among those in the boat, Bak Jonghoe, Mansan, Yi San and others were sick and could not work; Go Bojong, Yang Dalhae, Go Hoe, Kim Johoe, Im Sanhae and others, from the time of drifting at sea until this day, lay and did not stir, and though urged to bail out water and the like, they listened without attention; Jeong Sil, Bu Myeongdong, Kim Deuksi, Gang Yu, Song Jin, Kim Sok, Gang Nae, O San, Go Naeuldong and others answered one call out of ten, and some worked from necessity; So Geunbo, Kim Goesan, Go Bok, Kim Song, Kim Seokgwi, Yi Hyotae, Kim Jinsan and others were diligent by day and idle by night, or diligent at first and idle in the end; Heo Sangni, Gwon San, Kim Gomyeon, Kim Gujilhoe, Choe Geoisan, Kim Dojong, Go Ibok, Mun Hoe, Hyeonsan, Han Maesan, Gwon Song, Makgeum and others were not idle night or day and took the running of the boat as their own duty; Jeong Bo, Kim Jung, Yi Jeong, Son Hyoja, Yi Hyoji, An Ui and others either served in person or inspected and supervised the repair of the boat, hoping to see the task finished. After meeting the robbers and drifting again, people all had no heart to live, and gradually were not as before. The boat had been struck by violent waves for many days now and had a hundred holes and a thousand sores; as soon as one was plugged another gave way, and water leaked through the seams so that we could hardly manage to bail. I said: “The water leaks like this, and the men of the boat have slackened like this; if I presume arrogantly and sit watching us drown, how could that be?” And I, together with Jeong Bo and the others, six in all, myself scooped out almost all the water. Sangni and the others, ten or so, also somewhat roused themselves to rise. At night, without wind but with rain, we reached a large island but, thwarted by the tide, could not moor and lay in mid-stream on the sea.

paragraphs.orig: ## △十六日
paragraphs.en: 16th day

paragraphs.orig: 到泊於牛頭外洋。是日陰。海色赤黑中全濁。西望連峰疊嶂，撐天包海，意有人煙。駕東風而至，則見山上多有烽燧臺列峙，喜復到中國地界。午後，風浪尤緊，雨下濛昧，舟從風所驅。瞥然間，忽漂至兩島間，傍岸而過，則望見有中船六隻列泊。程保等請於臣曰：「前至下山，不示以官人之儀，以招賊人，幾不免死。今宜從權，具冠帶，以示彼船。」臣曰：「你何以害義之事導我歟？」保等曰：「當此之時，與死為鄰，何暇治禮義哉？姑當行權便，取生道，然後以禮治喪，不害於義。」臣拒之曰：「釋喪即吉，非孝也；以詐欺人，非信也。寧至於死，不忍處非孝非信之地，吾當順受以正。」安義來請曰：「我姑著此冠帶示若官人然。」臣曰：「非也。彼船若或如前所遇賊，猶之可也。若是好船，必驅我曹詣官府，取供詞，汝將何詞以對，少或不直，彼必生疑。莫如守正之為愈也。」俄而，所謂六船棹圍臣船。一船有人可八九，其衣服語音亦與下山所遇海賊一般，寫示臣等曰：「看你異類，來從那裏？」臣令程保亦寫以答曰：「我是朝鮮國朝臣，奉王事巡海島。奔喪過海，被風而來。不識此海何國地界？」其人答曰：「此海乃牛頭外洋，今隸大唐國台州府臨海縣界也。」程保以手指其口。其人以水桶來遺，又指北——有山——曰：「此山有泉，你可取汲，做飯以吃。你有胡椒可送我二三兩？」臣答曰：「本國不產胡椒，初不齎來。」其人等遂棹船稍卻，圍包臣船，列立下碇。臣船亦依岸而泊。令安義、巨伊山、尚理等下舟，登山通望人煙，則果是連陸處。
paragraphs.reading: 도박어우두외양. 시일음. 해색적흑중전탁. 서망련봉첩장, 탱천포해, 의유인연. 가동풍이지, 칙견산상다유봉수대열치, 희부도중국지계. 오후, 풍랑우긴, 우하몽매, 주종풍소구. 별연간, 홀표지양도간, 방안이과, 칙망견유중선육척열박. 정보등청어신왈: 「전지하산, 불시이관인지의, 이초적인, 기불면사. 금의종권, 구관대, 이시피선.」신왈: 「이하이해의지사도아여?」보등왈: 「당차지시, 여사위린, 하가치예의재? 고당행권편, 취생도, 연후이례치상, 불해어의.」신거지왈: 「석상즉길, 비효야; 이사기인, 비신야. 영지어사, 불인처비효비신지지, 오당순수이정.」안의래청왈: 「아고착차관대시약관인연.」신왈: 「비야. 피선약혹여전소우적, 유지가야. 약시호선, 필구아조예관부, 취공사, 여장하사이대, 소혹부직, 피필생의. 막여수정지위유야.」아이, 소위육선도위신선. 일선유인가팔구, 기의복어음역여하산소우해적일반, 사시신등왈: 「간이이류, 내종나리?」신영정보역사이답왈: 「아시조선국조신, 봉왕사순해도. 분상과해, 피풍이래. 불식차해하국지계?」기인답왈: 「차해내우두외양, 금례대당국태주부임해현계야.」정보이수지기구. 기인이수통래유, 우지북——유산——왈: 「차산유천, 이가취급, 주반이흘. 이유호초가송아이삼량?」신답왈: 「본국불산호초, 초부재래.」기인등수도선초각, 위포신선, 열립하정. 신선역의안이박. 영안의, 거이산, 상리등하주, 등산통망인연, 칙과시련륙처.
paragraphs.en: Anchored in the open sea off Niutou. That day overcast. The colour of the sea was reddish-black and wholly turbid. To the west, linked peaks and layered ranges propped up the sky and enfolded the sea; I thought there must be human habitation. Riding the east wind we came on, and saw beacon towers standing in rows on the mountains; I was glad to be at China’s border again. After noon the wind and waves grew stronger still, the rain came down misty and dim, and the boat was driven by the wind. In an instant we suddenly drifted between two islands and passed along the shore, and saw six medium-sized boats moored in a row. Jeong Bo and the others petitioned me: “Earlier, when we reached Xiashan, since we did not show the bearing of an official, we attracted robbers and almost did not escape death. Now we should follow expediency and put on cap and sash to show to those boats.” I said: “Why do you lead me with a thing that harms righteousness?” Bo and the others said: “At this time we are neighbours with death; what leisure have we to handle propriety? For now we should act expediently and take the way of life; then deal with the mourning according to rites, and it will not harm righteousness.” I refused them, saying: “To cast off mourning and put on the auspicious is not filial; to deceive people is not truthful. Rather than die, I cannot bear to be in a place that is neither filial nor truthful; I shall accept what comes with correctness.” An Ui came to ask: “For now I shall put on this cap and sash and appear as if I were an official.” I said: “No. If those boats are robbers as we met before, then so be it. But if they are good boats, they will surely drive us to the government office and take our depositions; what words will you use to answer? If there is the slightest crookedness, they will surely grow suspicious. Better to keep to uprightness.” Shortly the six boats came and sculled round my boat. One boat had eight or nine people, their clothing and speech the same as the sea-robbers met at Xiashan; they wrote and showed us: “We see you are of a different kind; where do you come from?” I had Jeong Bo write in reply: “I am a court official of the Kingdom of Joseon, who went by royal service to tour the islands. Hastening to a funeral I crossed the sea and was blown here by the wind. I do not know what country this sea belongs to.” The man replied: “This sea is the Niutou outer sea, now under the jurisdiction of Linhai County, Taizhou Prefecture, in the Great Tang.” Jeong Bo pointed with his hand to his mouth. The man sent over a bucket of water and pointed north — there was a hill — and said: “This hill has a spring; you can draw water and cook rice to eat. Do you have pepper? Send me two or three liang.” I answered: “Our country does not produce pepper, and I did not bring any at all.” The men then sculled their boats back a little, surrounded my boat, and standing in line dropped anchor. My boat too moored by the shore. I had An Ui, Geoisan, Sangni and others get off the boat and climb the hill to look out for human habitation; it was indeed land-connected.

paragraphs.orig: 臣於此行所歷滄波，雖若一海，水性水色隨處有異。濟州之海，色深青，性暴急，雖少風，濤上駕濤，激澓㶖㴸，無甚於此。至黑山島之西猶然。行過四晝夜，海色白；越二晝夜，愈白；又一晝夜，還青；又二晝夜，還白；又三晝夜，赤而濁；又一晝夜，赤黑中全濁。臣之行舟，視風從卻，東西南北，萍漂無定，其間所見海色大概如此。自白而還清以後，風力雖勁，濤不甚高。至還白以後，始有島礐」。島皆岩壁，谺𧯃礧砢，上戴土，有雜卉香草，蓊蔚長青；水性悠弱，若不遇大風，則罕見驚波駭浪之患。臣於遇賊復漂之海，亦如濟州之海之險，則豈能復見得島渚乎？
paragraphs.reading: 신어차행소력창파, 수약일해, 수성수색수처유이. 제주지해, 색심청, 성폭급, 수소풍, 도상가도, 격복㶖㴸, 무심어차. 지흑산도지서유연. 행과사주야, 해색백; 월이주야, 유백; 우일주야, 환청; 우이주야, 환백; 우삼주야, 적이탁; 우일주야, 적흑중전탁. 신지행주, 시풍종각, 동서남북, 평표무정, 기간소견해색대개여차. 자백이환청이후, 풍력수경, 도불심고. 지환백이후, 시유도각」. 도개암벽, 하𧯃뇌라, 상대토, 유잡훼향초, 옹울장청; 수성유약, 약불우대풍, 칙한견경파해랑지환. 신어우적부표지해, 역여제주지해지험, 칙기능부견득도저호?
paragraphs.en: Of the blue waves I passed through on this journey, although they seem a single sea, the nature and colour of the water differed from place to place. The sea of Jeju was deep blue and violent and swift in nature; even with little wind, wave rode upon wave, and surges roared and whirled — nothing is worse than this. It was still so to the west of Heuksan Island. After four days and nights of travel the colour of the sea was white; after two more days and nights, whiter still; after another day and night, blue again; after two more days and nights, white again; after three more days and nights, red and turbid; after another day and night, reddish-black and wholly turbid. My boat followed the wind, advancing and retreating, east, west, south and north, drifting like duckweed with no fixed course; the colour of the sea seen in between was roughly like this. After it went from white back to clear, although the wind was strong, the waves were not very high. After it turned white again, islands began to appear. The islands were all rock walls, yawning and rugged, bearing soil on top, with mixed flowers and fragrant plants, luxuriant and evergreen; the nature of the water was gentle and weak, and unless a great wind was met there was seldom the trouble of startling waves and frightening billows. Had the sea where I met the robbers and drifted again been as dangerous as the sea of Jeju, how could I have seen islets again?

paragraphs.orig: 大抵每歲正月，正當隆寒之極，冽風怒號，巨濤震激，乘船者所忌，——至二月，漸得風和。——濟州俗，猶號為燃燈節，禁不渡海。且江南潮人亦不於正月浮海。至四月，梅雨既過，颯然清風，海舶初回，謂之舶趕風。臣之漂海，適當風波險惡之時，海天霾噎，日復尤甚，檣帆維楫或折或失，饑渴困苦動經旬日，一日之間，溺敗之機非一二度矣。然幸僅保性命得泊海岸者，非特漬雨取汁以沃焦腸，舟實牢致儇駛，能壓風濤之故也。
paragraphs.reading: 대저매세정월, 정당융한지극, 열풍로호, 거도진격, 승선자소기, ——지이월, 점득풍화. ——제주속, 유호위연등절, 금부도해. 차강남조인역불어정월부해. 지사월, 매우기과, 삽연청풍, 해박초회, 위지박간풍. 신지표해, 적당풍파험오지시, 해천매열, 일부우심, 장범유즙혹절혹실, 기갈곤고동경순일, 일일지간, 익패지기비일이도의. 연행근보성명득박해안자, 비특지우취즙이옥초장, 주실뇌치현사, 능압풍도지고야.
paragraphs.en: In general, the first month of every year is precisely the extreme of the great cold, when freezing winds howl in rage and huge waves surge; it is what travellers by ship shun — by the second month the wind gradually becomes mild. The custom in Jeju still calls it the “Lantern-lighting Festival” and forbids crossing the sea. Moreover, the sea-faring people of the tidal regions south of the Yangzi also do not put to sea in the first month. In the fourth month, when the plum rains have passed, a brisk cool wind arrives; when sea-going ships first turn back, it is called the “ship-chasing wind.” My drifting on the sea happened to fall in a time of dangerous winds and waves; sea and sky were dark and choked, worse each day; masts, sails, ropes and oars were broken or lost; hunger, thirst and hardship lasted ten days at a time; in the space of one day the moments of drowning and wreck were not once or twice. Yet that I barely preserved my life and was able to anchor on the coast of the sea was not only because we soaked rain into clothing and took the juice to pour on parched bowels, but because the boat was truly sturdy and fast and could press down wind and waves.

paragraphs.orig: ## △十七日
paragraphs.en: 17th day

paragraphs.orig: 舍舟登陸。是日雨。遲明，所謂六船擁來，語臣等曰：「看你也是好人，隨我可行。你有奇物送些與我。」臣答曰：「漂流已久，所齎之物盡撒海中。若指我生路，所乘船楫皆恁的所有。」因問人居遠近。其一人曰：「此地也近官府，你要去，不妨。」一人曰：「過前一里便有人家。」一人曰：「此處人家便遠，不可止此。」，臣又問：「官路遠近？」其一人曰：「台州府距此一百八十里。」一人曰：「一百五十里」。一人曰：「二百四十里。」其語端彼此有違，不可信也。其人等相率鬧擾，爭入臣船，目所寓雖些小物，無不攘奪。謂臣等曰：「不同我去，我當作怒。」安義請舍船，乘其人船隨，其所去。李楨欲擊殺一人以卻之。臣曰：「爾等之計皆非也。觀彼人其言不實，劫奪又甚，情偽淺深未可知也。彼若昔者下山海賊之類，則從安義之計而從歸，則彼必掉至絕島，沉殺我等以滅其跡。彼若或漁船，若防禦之船，則從李楨之計而擊殺，則彼必掩其所為，反以我為異國人來劫殺人云爾，則大國之邊境騷然，誣我為賊，語且不通，難以辨明，必皆為邊將所戳。爾等之計皆自取死途也，莫若權詞以觀其勢。」臣謂其人曰：「我浮海日多，饑渴困憊之極，危命僅一線耳。請做飯療饑，然後同行。」其人等復曰：「你少留緩行。」即棹舟少卻可二三里許，復環臣船而泊。以雨故皆入船倉中，無觀望者。
paragraphs.reading: 사주등륙. 시일우. 지명, 소위육선옹래, 어신등왈: 「간이야시호인, 수아가행. 이유기물송사여아.」신답왈: 「표류이구, 소재지물진살해중. 약지아생로, 소승선즙개임적소유.」인문인거원근. 기일인왈: 「차지야근관부, 이요거, 불방.」일인왈: 「과전일리편유인가.」일인왈: 「차처인가편원, 불가지차.」, 신우문: 「관로원근?」기일인왈: 「태주부거차일백팔십리.」일인왈: 「일백오십리」. 일인왈: 「이백사십리.」기어단피차유위, 불가신야. 기인등상솔요요, 쟁입신선, 목소우수사소물, 무불양탈. 위신등왈: 「부동아거, 아당작로.」안의청사선, 승기인선수, 기소거. 이정욕격살일인이각지. 신왈: 「이등지계개비야. 관피인기언불실, 겁탈우심, 정위천심미가지야. 피약석자하산해적지류, 칙종안의지계이종귀, 칙피필도지절도, 침살아등이멸기적. 피약혹어선, 약방어지선, 칙종이정지계이격살, 칙피필엄기소위, 반이아위이국인래겁살인운이, 칙대국지변경소연, 무아위적, 어차불통, 난이변명, 필개위변장소착. 이등지계개자취사도야, 막약권사이관기세.」신위기인왈: 「아부해일다, 기갈곤비지극, 위명근일선이. 청주반요기, 연후동행.」기인등부왈: 「이소류완행.」즉도주소각가이삼리허, 부환신선이박. 이우고개입선창중, 무관망자.
paragraphs.en: Left the boat and landed. That day rain. At first light the six boats came crowding and said to us: “We see you are good people; follow us and you can go.
