paragraphs.en: Those who are robbers kill and plunder people for goods, and rampage without restraint. Though the people of Jiangnan today may sometimes be driven by greed to become robbers and plunderers, still the robbers of Xiashan did not kill us and also left things behind; the people of Xianyan did not conceal what they had plundered and in the end returned the saddle — from which one can see the gentleness of the local mood and that people’s hearts are not very cruel and evil.

paragraphs.orig: ## △二十四日
paragraphs.en: 24th day

paragraphs.orig: 至健跳所。是日晴。曉，過穿岩里。里西有山，戴石壁屹立，穹隆有大竇洞，望如虹門，里之得名以此。又過田嶺，嶺上有僧作佛宇橫道，路行人從寺中以過。臣等平地雖或乘轎，嶺峻路險，下轎步行為多。至此寺，百技跛行，寺僧憐之，煎茶以供，少留。行至海浦，有兵船，具戎器，循浦上下，示以水戰之狀。臣從鼻居舠以渡，則乃是健跳所也。城臨海岸，所千戶李昂軀幹壯大，容儀豐美，具甲胄兵戎，導臣等入城門。門皆重城，鼓角、銃熥聲震海嶽。其嗩呐等大小角末端皆上曲，鉤向吹者眉目間。城中人物、第宅視桃渚所尤豐盛。李昂引臣至一客館，與翟勇、許清、王匡、王海等及所之有姓莊也、尹也——亡其名，俱是厚重老官人，——皆環立桌之左右，問臣以漂流之故。臣略陳首末云云。李昂請升堂，行賓主之禮。昂由西階，臣由東階而上，相對再拜後，昂饋臣茶果，又饋臣之從者以酒肉，頗示忠款之意。姓尹老官人引程保等詣私第飲食之，因見其妻妾子女以展禮。其人心淳龐如此。有一人，以丙午年登科小錄來示臣，曰：「此吾的登科第榜錄也。」又指點錄中張輔二字曰：「此吾的姓名也。」因問曰：「你國亦貴其登科者乎？」曰：「然。」曰：「我國制，草茅士登第者，皆官給俸祿，旌表門閭，刺銜，亦書賜進士及第某科某等人」云云。引臣至其家，則其家前街果以雕龍石柱作二層三間之門，金碧眩曜，其上大書「丙午科張輔之家」之標。輔蓋以己之登第誇示臣。臣亦以浮誕之言誇之曰：「我再中科第，歲受米二百石，旌門三層，足下其不及於我矣。」輔曰：「何以知之？」臣曰：「我之旌門遠莫致之。我有文科重試小錄在此。」即撥示之。輔於錄中見臣職姓名，下跪曰：「我殆不及矣。」
paragraphs.reading: 지건도소. 시일청. 효, 과천암리. 이서유산, 대석벽흘립, 궁륭유대두동, 망여홍문, 이지득명이차. 우과전령, 영상유승작불우횡도, 노행인종사중이과. 신등평지수혹승교, 영준로험, 하교보행위다. 지차사, 백기파행, 사승연지, 전다이공, 소류. 행지해포, 유병선, 구융기, 순포상하, 시이수전지상. 신종비거도이도, 칙내시건도소야. 성임해안, 소천호이앙구간장대, 용의풍미, 구갑주병융, 도신등입성문. 문개중성, 고각, 총통성진해악. 기쇄눌등대소각말단개상곡, 구향취자미목간. 성중인물, 제택시도저소우풍성. 이앙인신지일객관, 여적용, 허청, 왕광, 왕해등급소지유성장야, 윤야——망기명, 구시후중노관인, ——개환입탁지좌우, 문신이표류지고. 신약진수말운운. 이앙청승당, 행빈주지례. 앙유서계, 신유동계이상, 상대재배후, 앙궤신다과, 우궤신지종자이주육, 파시충관지의. 성윤노관인인정보등예사제음식지, 인견기처첩자녀이전례. 기인심순방여차. 유일인, 이병오년등과소록래시신, 왈: 「차오적등과제방록야.」우지점록중장보이자왈: 「차오적성명야.」인문왈: 「이국역귀기등과자호?」왈: 「연.」왈: 「아국제, 초모사등제자, 개관급봉록, 정표문려, 자함, 역서사진사급제모과모등인」운운. 인신지기가, 칙기가전가과이조룡석주작이층삼간지문, 금벽현요, 기상대서「병오과장보지가」지표. 보개이기지등제과시신. 신역이부탄지언과지왈: 「아재중과제, 세수미이백석, 정문삼층, 족하기불급어아의.」보왈: 「하이지지?」신왈: 「아지정문원막치지. 아유문과중시소록재차.」즉발시지. 보어록중견신직성명, 하궤왈: 「아태불급의.」
paragraphs.en: Reached Jiantiao Garrison. That day fair. At dawn we passed Chuanyan village. West of the village was a mountain, bearing a rock cliff standing sheer, arched with a great cave, which looked like a rainbow gate from afar; the village got its name from this. We then passed Tian Ridge, on which monks had built a Buddhist temple across the road, so that road-walkers passed through the temple. Although on level ground we sometimes rode in chairs, on steep ridges and perilous roads we mostly got down and walked. Reaching this temple, with all our joints sore and limping, the temple monks pitied us and boiled tea to offer; we rested a while. Going on to a sea inlet, there were warships, equipped with weapons, going up and down along the inlet, showing the appearance of naval battle. I crossed by tender boat, and it was Jiantiao Garrison. The town faced the sea shore; the Qianhu Li Ang, large and strong of frame, handsome and dignified in bearing, in armour and weapons, led us into the town gate. The gates were all double walls, and the sound of drums, horns and guns shook the seas and mountains. The ends of the suona and other large and small horns all curved upward, hooked toward the eyes of the blower. The people and houses in the town were even more abundant and flourishing than at Taozhu Garrison. Li Ang led me to a guest lodge, and with Zhai Yong, Xu Qing, Wang Kuang, Wang Hai and others, and those present surnamed Zhuang and Yin — I have lost their names, both old officials of weighty and kindly character — all stood in a ring at the left and right sides of the table and asked me about the reason for my drift. I briefly told them from beginning to end, and so on. Li Ang invited me to ascend the hall and performed the rite of guest and host. Ang went up by the west steps and I by the east steps, and facing each other we bowed twice; then Ang offered me tea and fruit and offered my followers wine and meat, showing great sincerity. The old official surnamed Yin led Jeong Bo and the others to his private house to eat and drink, and had them meet his wives, concubines, sons and daughters to pay their respects. His heart was so gentle and generous. A man showed me a register of the Bingwu-year examination graduates, saying: “This is the list of my passing the examination.” He pointed to the two characters Zhang Fu in the register and said: “This is my name.” And he asked: “Does your country also honour those who pass the examination?” “Yes.” He said: “By our country’s system, scholars from humble thatched homes who pass are all given a salary by the government, have their gates honoured with banners, and on their calling cards also write ‘Granted jinshi degree, such class, such rank,’” and so on. He led me to his house, and in front of his house on the street there was indeed a two-storey, three-bay gate with carved dragon stone pillars, dazzling with gold and blue-green, with the large inscription above: “House of Zhang Fu of the Bingwu Examination.” Fu evidently wished to boast to me of his own passing. I too boasted with vainglorious words: “I passed twice, and each year receive two hundred seok of rice, and have a gate honoured with three storeys; you cannot match me.” Fu said: “How do you know?” I said: “My honoured gate is too far to bring here. But I have the record of the literary re-examination here.” I opened it and showed him. Fu, seeing in the record my office and name, knelt and said: “I am no match for you.”

paragraphs.orig: ## △二十五日
paragraphs.en: 25th day

paragraphs.orig: 到越溪巡檢司。是日陰霾。李昂、許清、王匡及莊也、尹也，俱送臣於海上。昂握臣手曰：「我與足下千載一時，萬里一見，一別兩地，無復再見。」臣於船上敘別曰：「僕之來也，將軍以百千兵甲環城擁闠，旌旗淩亂，錚鼓轟馳，則將軍之示遠人嚴矣；僕之寓館也，升堂禮莫愆，饋食意益彌，開心見誠，一見如舊，則將軍之待遠人寬矣；及僕之去也，步出城西，遠送海曲，扶僕登船，敘辭以別，則將軍之送遠人厚矣。僕一遠人也，相逢未一日也，而嚴以示之，寬以待之，厚以別之，其意固有在也。蓋我朝鮮地雖海外，衣冠文物悉同中國，則不可以外國視也。況今大明一統，胡越為家，則一天之下皆吾兄弟，豈以地之遠近分內外哉？況又我國恪事天朝，貢獻不怠，故天子亦禮以待之，仁以扶之，懷綏之化至矣，盡矣！而僕朝鮮之臣也，將軍亦天子分閫之臣也，則其體天子字小之心，而待遠人至於此極，斯不亦忠矣乎哉！其間情意之篤，則僕既感之深矣。然不得一日之暇，與將軍及莊、尹兩官人從容談話，展布所懷。百歲之間，萬里之外，雲樹之望，曷維其已。」又別許清曰：「將軍與王足下匡，遇我於蒲峰之里，飽我於饑渴之極，生我於萬死之餘。以至杜瀆場，以至桃渚所，以至於此城，崎嶇數百里之地，扶護七八日之間，其恩情之篤，不勝枚悉。一別之後，會面難期，衹增黯然。」遂告別，與翟勇同舟過大海。勇謂臣曰：「浮此海而去，西可望天台山，今適雲霧四塞，不得觀望」云云。夕，至寧海縣之越溪巡檢司。城在山巔，軍卒皆帶甲列立海旁。勇與其徒下舟入城，留臣等於海岸，莫知所為。
paragraphs.reading: 도월계순검사. 시일음매. 이앙, 허청, 왕광급장야, 윤야, 구송신어해상. 앙악신수왈: 「아여족하천재일시, 만리일견, 일별양지, 무부재견.」신어선상서별왈: 「복지래야, 장군이백천병갑환성옹궤, 정기능란, 쟁고굉치, 칙장군지시원인엄의; 복지우관야, 승당예막건, 궤식의익미, 개심견성, 일견여구, 칙장군지대원인관의; 급복지거야, 보출성서, 원송해곡, 부복등선, 서사이별, 칙장군지송원인후의. 복일원인야, 상봉미일일야, 이엄이시지, 관이대지, 후이별지, 기의고유재야. 개아조선지수해외, 의관문물실동중국, 칙불가이외국시야. 황금대명일통, 호월위가, 칙일천지하개오형제, 기이지지원근분내외재? 황우아국각사천조, 공헌불태, 고천자역예이대지, 인이부지, 회수지화지의, 진의! 이복조선지신야, 장군역천자분곤지신야, 칙기체천자자소지심, 이대원인지어차극, 사불역충의호재! 기간정의지독, 칙복기감지심의. 연부득일일지가, 여장군급장, 윤양관인종용담화, 전포소회. 백세지간, 만리지외, 운수지망, 갈유기이.」우별허청왈: 「장군여왕족하광, 우아어포봉지리, 포아어기갈지극, 생아어만사지여. 이지두독장, 이지도저소, 이지어차성, 기구수백리지지, 부호칠팔일지간, 기은정지독, 불승매실. 일별지후, 회면난기, 기증암연.」수고별, 여적용동주과대해. 용위신왈: 「부차해이거, 서가망천태산, 금적운무사색, 부득관망」운운. 석, 지영해현지월계순검사. 성재산전, 군졸개대갑열립해방. 용여기도하주입성, 유신등어해안, 막지소위.
paragraphs.en: Arrived at the Yuexi Inspectorate. That day overcast and murky. Li Ang, Xu Qing, Wang Kuang, and Zhuang and Yin all saw me off to the sea. Ang held my hand and said: “You and I — a once in a thousand years chance, a meeting across ten thousand li; once parted, in two places, we shall never meet again.” From the boat I bade farewell with these words: “When I came, General, you ringed the city with a hundred thousand armoured soldiers and crowded the streets, banners tumbling in disorder, gongs and drums thundering — so the General showed me, a man from afar, his sternness. When I lodged, I ascended the hall and the rites were not at fault; you offered food and your meaning grew ever deeper; you opened your heart and showed sincerity, and at first meeting it was like old friends — so the General treated me, a man from afar, with generosity. And at my departure you walked out of the west of the city, saw me off far to the bend of the sea, helped me onto the boat, and spoke words of parting — so the General sent off a man from afar with warmth. I am one man from afar, we had not met even one day, and yet you showed me sternness, treated me with generosity, and parted from me with warmth; there must be a purpose in it. For though my Joseon is a land beyond the sea, our dress, caps and culture are all the same as China’s, so I should not be regarded as from a foreign country. Moreover now that the Great Ming is unified, taking Hu and Yue as one household, all under one heaven are my brothers; how could one divide inner from outer by the distance of land? Moreover our country serves the Heavenly Court reverently and presents tribute without slackness, so the Son of Heaven too treats it with courtesy and supports it with benevolence; the transforming influence of his comfort and pacification is complete and exhaustive! And I am a subject of Joseon, and the General too is a subject of the Son of Heaven entrusted with a command of the frontier; so in embodying the Son of Heaven’s heart of cherishing the small and treating a man from afar to this extent — is that not loyalty indeed! The depth of your feeling in the meantime I have already been deeply moved by. Yet I have not had a single day’s leisure to talk at ease with the General and the two officials Zhuang and Yin and to unfold what is in my heart. Across a hundred years, beyond ten thousand li, gazing at clouds and trees — when will it end?” I took leave of Xu Qing also, saying: “General, together with Mr. Wang Kuang, you met me in Pufeng village, fed me at the extreme of hunger and thirst, and brought me to life after ten thousand deaths. From Dudu Yard to Taozhu Garrison and to this town, over several hundred li of rugged ground, for seven or eight days you supported and protected me; your kindness cannot be counted. After one parting a meeting is hard to expect, and it only deepens my sorrow.” So I took my leave and, with Zhai Yong, crossed the great sea in the same boat. Yong said to me: “Sailing this sea and going on, to the west you can see Mt. Tiantai, but now clouds and fog fill the four quarters and we cannot look,” and so on. In the evening we reached the Yuexi Inspectorate in Ninghai County. The town was on a mountain top, and soldiers all stood in armour in a row by the sea. Yong and his companions got off the boat and entered the town, leaving us on the shore, and we knew not what to do.

paragraphs.orig: ## △二十六日
paragraphs.en: 26th day

paragraphs.orig: 過寧海縣。是日雨。巡檢司對岸有越溪鋪。自鋪前舍舟乘陸，從溪岸而步。溪之通海口甚廣闊，不知其源之所從來。行過西洋嶺、許家山，至市奧鋪，鋪中人饋茶數碗。又行至白嶠嶺，有軍卒二十餘人擔轎來迎臣等，臣等八人又乘。過進士坊，至寧海縣之白嶠驛，驛在縣治之中。有知縣姓唐者，供饋臣等，期至於飽。因乘轎冒雨而行，過桐山鋪、梅林鋪、江漩嶺、缸窯鋪、海口鋪。其間有三大川、二大橋，亡其名。夜二更，至西店驛以宿。驛有甲兵警戍，如防禦所。
paragraphs.reading: 과영해현. 시일우. 순검사대안유월계포. 자포전사주승륙, 종계안이보. 계지통해구심광활, 부지기원지소종래. 행과서양령, 허가산, 지시오포, 포중인궤다수완. 우행지백교령, 유군졸이십여인담교래영신등, 신등팔인우승. 과진사방, 지영해현지백교역, 역재현치지중. 유지현성당자, 공궤신등, 기지어포. 인승교모우이행, 과동산포, 매림포, 강선령, 항요포, 해구포. 기간유삼대천, 이대교, 망기명. 야이경, 지서점역이숙. 역유갑병경수, 여방어소.
paragraphs.en: Passed Ninghai County. That day rain. Opposite the shore of the Inspectorate was Yuexi Post. In front of the post we left the boat and took to land, going on foot along the stream bank. The stream’s mouth to the sea was very wide, and I knew not where its source came from. Going on past Xiyang Ridge and Xujia Hill, we reached Shi’ao Post, where the people in the post offered several bowls of tea. Going on to Baijiao Ridge, more than twenty soldiers carrying sedan chairs came to meet us, and the eight of us rode again. Passing the Jinshi Archway, we came to Baijiao Station in Ninghai County, which was within the county seat. The magistrate, surnamed Tang, provided for us until we were full. We then rode on in chairs through the rain, passing Tongshan Post, Meilin Post, Jiangxuan Ridge, Gangyao Post and Haikou Post. In between were three large rivers and two large bridges, whose names I have lost. At the second watch of the night we reached Xidian Station and lodged. The station had armoured soldiers on guard, like a defensive post.

paragraphs.orig: ## △二十七日
paragraphs.en: 27th day

paragraphs.orig: 在西店驛。是日大風大雨。溪澗水漲，不得已留於西店驛。
paragraphs.reading: 재서점역. 시일대풍대우. 계간수창, 부득이류어서점역.
paragraphs.en: At Xidian Station. That day great wind and great rain. The streams swelled, and we had no choice but to stay at Xidian Station.

paragraphs.orig: ## △二十八日
paragraphs.en: 28th day

paragraphs.orig: 到連山驛。是日大雨。翟勇謂臣曰：「我大唐法令嚴整，少有遲緩必致罪責，今雖大雨不可復留。」勇之軍吏及臣之從者俱不欲，曰：「今日雨大至，水溢洞壑，不可行！」勇曰：「洞壑潦水，滿而復除，且此驛支給亦有限量，昨日之留已為不可。」遂與臣等冒雨過珊墟鋪、拆開嶺、山隍鋪，又過大嶺、方門鋪至雙溪鋪。鋪北有雙溪，溪水漲溢，人皆以衣而涉。經尚田鋪，止宿奉化縣之連山驛。縣距驛東二里。知縣姓名杜安也。驛丞見臣等雨透沾衣，肌寒帶粟，遂煨榾拙於堂前。臣及從者環坐，親灸使自溫。有一人自外至，橫怒肆毒，蹴踏榾拙之火。臣等惴懼奔匿。勇及驛丞俱被辱焉。勇謂臣曰：「外有一人說你是劫賊之人，阻擋驛官不要供給。我與他說汝是讀書君子。他復肆暴。你可寫狀告他搶去衣包云云，呈於知縣。」臣曰：「彼人之惡，誠欲可懲，但以不見奪之物誣為強奪，伏人非罪，甚悖於理。今足下護我等而來，治他以喝眾侵暴之罪，亦不為無詞。」勇即寫狀，送於縣官。
paragraphs.reading: 도연산역. 시일대우. 적용위신왈: 「아대당법령엄정, 소유지완필치죄책, 금수대우불가부류.」용지군리급신지종자구불욕, 왈: 「금일우대지, 수일동학, 불가행!」용왈: 「동학요수, 만이부제, 차차역지급역유한량, 작일지류이위불가.」수여신등모우과산허포, 탁개령, 산황포, 우과대령, 방문포지쌍계포. 포북유쌍계, 계수창일, 인개이의이섭. 경상전포, 지숙봉화현지연산역. 현거역동이리. 지현성명두안야. 역승견신등우투첨의, 기한대속, 수외골졸어당전. 신급종자환좌, 친구사자온. 유일인자외지, 횡로사독, 축답골졸지화. 신등췌구분닉. 용급역승구피욕언. 용위신왈: 「외유일인설이시겁적지인, 조당역관불요공급. 아여타설여시독서군자. 타부사포. 이가사상고타창거의포운운, 정어지현.」신왈: 「피인지악, 성욕가징, 단이불견탈지물무위강탈, 복인비죄, 심패어리. 금족하호아등이래, 치타이갈중침포지죄, 역불위무사.」용즉사상, 송어현관.
paragraphs.en: Reached Lianshan Station. That day heavy rain. Zhai Yong said to me: “Our Great Tang’s laws and orders are strict and orderly; the slightest delay brings punishment. Though it rains heavily today, we cannot stay again.” Yong’s military clerks and my followers all did not want to go, saying: “The rain has come in torrents today, and water overflows the gullies; we cannot travel!” Yong said: “The flood water in the gullies fills and then drains away; moreover the supplies of this station are limited, and staying yesterday was already improper.” So with us he went through the rain past Shanxu Post, Chaikai Ridge and Shanhuang Post, then over a great ridge, and past Fangmen Post to Shuangxi Post. North of the post were twin streams; the stream water was flooding, and everyone waded across in their clothes. We passed Shangtian Post and halted for the night at Lianshan Station in Fenghua County. The county seat is two li east of the station. The magistrate’s name was Du An. The station master, seeing us soaked through by the rain, our flesh cold and goose-pimpled, lit a fire of logs in front of the hall. I and my followers sat around it and warmed ourselves in person. A man came from outside, angrily and cruelly kicked and trampled the log fire. We were frightened and fled to hide. Yong and the station master were both insulted. Yong said to me: “Someone outside says you are a robber, and is blocking the station officer from supplying you. I told him that you are a scholar, a gentleman. He again behaved violently. You can write a statement accusing him of snatching away your clothing bundle, and submit it to the magistrate.” I said: “That man’s wickedness truly deserves punishment, but to falsely call a thing not taken a robbery and put an innocent man at fault is much against reason. Now that you have protected us and come, punishing him for the offence of shouting at the crowd and assaulting us is also not without a pretext.” Yong at once wrote the statement and sent it to the county officer.

paragraphs.orig: ## △二十九日
paragraphs.en: 29th day

paragraphs.orig: 過寧波府。是日雨。翟勇與臣等乘轎過大川。川畔有佛宇，極華麗，前有五浮圖、雙大塔。又過虛白觀、金鐘鋪、南渡鋪，至廣濟橋。橋跨大川，橋上架屋，橋長可二十餘步。橋所在之地即寧波府界，舊為明州時所建也。又行至三里，有大橋，橋之北有進士里。又行至十餘里，又有大橋，橋上亦架屋，與廣濟橋同而差小，忘其名。橋之南有文秀鄉。又過常浦橋至北渡江，乘小舶而渡。自牛頭外洋西北至連山驛，群峰列岫糾紛繚繞，溪澗岩壁縈紆錯亂。至此江，則平郊廣野一望豁如，但見遠山如眉耳。江之北岸築一壩，壩即挽舟上過之處。壩之北築堤，鑿江，有鼻居舠繞岸列泊。勇引臣等乘其舠過石橋十三，行二十餘里。江之東堤，閭閻撲地。其西南望有四明山。山西南連天台山，東北連會稽、秦望等山，即賀知章少時所居也。棹至寧波府城，截流築城，城皆重門，門皆重層，門外重城，水溝亦重。城皆設虹門，門有鐵扃，可容一船。棹入城中，至尚書橋，橋內江廣可一百餘步。又過惠政橋、社稷壇。凡城中所過大橋亦不止十餘處，高宮巨室，夾岸聯絡，紫石為柱者，殆居其半，奇觀勝景不可殫錄。棹出北門，門亦與南門同。城周廣狹不可知。府治及寧波衛、鄞縣治及四明驛，俱在城中。至過大得橋，橋有三虹門。雨甚，留泊江中。
paragraphs.reading: 과영파부. 시일우. 적용여신등승교과대천. 천반유불우, 극화려, 전유오부도, 쌍대탑. 우과허백관, 금종포, 남도포, 지광제교. 교과대천, 교상가옥, 교장가이십여보. 교소재지지즉영파부계, 구위명주시소건야. 우행지삼리, 유대교, 교지북유진사리. 우행지십여리, 우유대교, 교상역가옥, 여광제교동이차소, 망기명. 교지남유문수향. 우과상포교지북도강, 승소박이도. 자우두외양서북지연산역, 군봉열수규분료요, 계간암벽영우착란. 지차강, 칙평교광야일망활여, 단견원산여미이. 강지북안축일파, 파즉만주상과지처. 파지북축제, 착강, 유비거도요안열박. 용인신등승기도과석교십삼, 행이십여리. 강지동제, 여염박지. 기서남망유사명산. 산서남련천태산, 동북련회계, 진망등산, 즉하지장소시소거야. 도지영파부성, 절류축성, 성개중문, 문개중층, 문외중성, 수구역중. 성개설홍문, 문유철경, 가용일선. 도입성중, 지상서교, 교내강광가일백여보. 우과혜정교, 사직단. 범성중소과대교역부지십여처, 고궁거실, 협안연락, 자석위주자, 태거기반, 기관승경불가탄록. 도출북문, 문역여남문동. 성주광협불가지. 부치급영파위, 은현치급사명역, 구재성중. 지과대득교, 교유삼홍문. 우심, 유박강중.
paragraphs.en: Passed Ningbo Prefecture. That day rain. Zhai Yong and we rode in sedan chairs across a large river. On the river bank was a Buddhist temple, extremely splendid, with five pagodas in front and twin great towers. We passed the Xubai Temple, Jinzhong Post and Nandu Post, and reached Guangji Bridge. The bridge spans the large river, and houses are built on the bridge; the bridge is twenty-odd paces long. The place where the bridge stands is at the boundary of Ningbo Prefecture, and it was built in the time when it was Mingzhou. Going three li further there was a large bridge, north of which was Jinshi village. Going more than ten li further there was another large bridge, with houses built on it too, the same as Guangji Bridge but a little smaller; I have forgotten its name. South of the bridge was Wenxiu district. We then passed Changpu Bridge and came to the North Ferry on the river, and crossed in a small boat. From the Niutou outer sea north-west to Lianshan Station, groups of peaks and rows of ridges tangled and wound, and streams and rock walls coiled and interlaced. On reaching this river, the level fields and wide plains opened wide to view, and one saw only distant hills like eyebrows. On the north bank of the river a dam had been built, the place where boats are hauled up and over. North of the dam a bank was built and the river was dug out, and tender boats were moored in rows along the shore. Yong led us to ride in the tender, passing thirteen stone bridges and going twenty-odd li. Along the east bank of the river, villages spread across the ground. Looking south-west one could see Mt. Siming. West and south it joins Mt. Tiantai, and north-east it joins Kuaiji, Qinwang and other mountains, where He Zhizhang lived in his youth. We sculled to the city of Ningbo Prefecture; the city had been built cutting across the stream, its walls all with double gates, the gates all double-storeyed, outside the gates double walls, and the moats also double. The city all had rainbow-arched gates, each with iron bars, wide enough for a boat. We sculled into the city, to Shangshu Bridge, inside which the river was a hundred paces or more wide. Then we passed Huizheng Bridge and the Altar of the Soil and Grain. The large bridges passed in the city were more than ten; tall palaces and great houses lined the banks in unbroken rows, and those with purple stone pillars were nearly half; wonderful sights and fine scenes cannot be recorded in full. We sculled out of the north gate, which was the same as the south gate. The perimeter of the city, large or small, I could not know. The prefectural office, the Ningbo Guard, the office of Yin County and Siming Station were all inside the city. We passed Dade Bridge, which had three arched openings, but the rain was heavy and we stayed and moored in the river.

paragraphs.orig: ## △二月初一日
paragraphs.en: Second month, 1st day

paragraphs.orig: 過慈溪縣。是日雨。經新清橋、進士鄉，至宋石將軍廟。廟大如官府，立旌表之門。自府城至此十餘里間，江之兩岸，市肆、舸艦坌集如雲。過此後，松篁橙桔夾岸成林。又過茶亭、景安鋪、繼錦鄉、俞氏貞節門，至西鎮橋，橋高大。所過又有二大橋，至西壩廳。壩之兩岸築堤，以石斷流為堰，使與外江不得相通，兩旁設機械，以竹為纜，挽舟而過。至西璵鄉之新堰，堰舊為刹子港顏公堰，後塞，港廢，堰為田。導水東彙至於廣利橋之南。置此壩，外捍江湖，挽濟官船，謂之新堰，概與西壩同。至此，又挽舟而過，過新橋、開禧橋、姚平處士之墓，至慈溪縣。棹入其中，有經元門、鍾英門、都堂里門、都憲橋、進士門、德星橋、寶峰門，至臨清亭前少停舟。夜，又溯江而北，至雞報，泊於岸待曙。而問其江，則乃姚江也。江邊有驛，乃車廄驛也。驛丞乃秦高也。
paragraphs.reading: 과자계현. 시일우. 경신청교, 진사향, 지송석장군묘. 묘대여관부, 입정표지문. 자부성지차십여리간, 강지양안, 시사, 가함분집여운. 과차후, 송황등길협안성림. 우과다정, 경안포, 계금향, 유씨정절문, 지서진교, 교고대. 소과우유이대교, 지서파청. 파지양안축제, 이석단류위언, 사여외강부득상통, 양방설기계, 이죽위람, 만주이과. 지서여향지신언, 언구위찰자항안공언, 후색, 항폐, 언위전. 도수동휘지어광리교지남. 치차파, 외한강호, 만제관선, 위지신언, 개여서파동. 지차, 우만주이과, 과신교, 개희교, 요평처사지묘, 지자계현. 도입기중, 유경원문, 종영문, 도당리문, 도헌교, 진사문, 덕성교, 보봉문, 지임청정전소정주. 야, 우소강이북, 지계보, 박어안대서. 이문기강, 칙내요강야. 강변유역, 내차구역야. 역승내진고야.
paragraphs.en: Passed Cixi County. That day rain. Passing New Qing Bridge and Jinshi village, we reached the Temple of General Song Shi. The temple was as large as a government office and had an honorific gate erected. From the prefectural city to here, over ten li, on both banks of the river, markets and boats crowded together like clouds. After this, pines, bamboos, oranges and tangerines lined the banks and formed forests. We passed also the Tea Pavilion, Jing’an Post, Jijin district, the Yu family’s Chastity Gate, and reached Xizhen Bridge, which was tall and large. We passed two more large bridges and reached the Xiba Hall. On both banks of the dam, banks were built; with stone the stream was cut off to make a weir, so that it could not connect with the outer river; on both sides machines were set up, and with bamboo ropes boats were hauled over. At the New Weir of Xiyu district, the weir used to be Yan Gong Weir at Chazi Harbour, which later silted up, the harbour was abandoned, and the weir became fields. Water was led to gather eastward to the south of Guangli Bridge. This dam was set up to keep out the river and lake outside and haul government boats across; it was called the New Weir, and generally the same as the Western Dam. Here again we were hauled over; then we passed Xin Bridge, Kaixi Bridge and the tomb of the retired scholar Yao Ping, and reached Cixi County. We sculled into it, passing the Jingyuan Gate, Zhongying Gate, Dutang village gate, Duxian Bridge, Jinshi Gate, Dexing Bridge and Baofeng Gate, and stopped the boat briefly in front of Linqing Pavilion. At night we again went up the river northward, as far as Jibao, and moored at the bank waiting for dawn. Asked, the river was the Yao River. By the river was a station, which was Chejiu Station. The station master was Qin Gao.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初二日
paragraphs.en: 2nd day

paragraphs.orig: 過餘姚縣。是日陰。早，發船溯西北而上。江山高大，郊野平鋪，人煙稠密，景物萬千。日夕，過五靈廟、驛前鋪，姚江驛、江橋，至餘姚縣。江抱城而西，有聯錦鄉、曹墅橋，橋三虹門。又過登科門、張氏光明堂，夜三更到下新壩，壩又與前所見新堰同。又挽舟過壩，經一大橋，有大樹數十株列立江中。將曙，到中壩，壩又與下新壩同。又挽舟逆上，江即上虞江也。
paragraphs.reading: 과여요현. 시일음. 조, 발선소서북이상. 강산고대, 교야평포, 인연조밀, 경물만천. 일석, 과오령묘, 역전포, 요강역, 강교, 지여요현. 강포성이서, 유연금향, 조서교, 교삼홍문. 우과등과문, 장씨광명당, 야삼경도하신파, 파우여전소견신언동. 우만주과파, 경일대교, 유대수수십주열립강중. 장서, 도중파, 파우여하신파동. 우만주역상, 강즉상우강야.
paragraphs.en: Passed Yuyao County. That day overcast. Early, we set out by boat, going up north-west. The rivers and hills were high and great, the countryside spread flat, the human smoke dense, the scenes in ten thousand varieties. At dusk we passed the Wuling Temple, Yiqian Post, Yaojiang Station and Jiang Bridge, and reached Yuyao County. The river embraced the city and went west; there were Lianjin district and Caoshu Bridge, a bridge with three arches. We passed also the Dengke Gate and the Zhang family’s Guangming Hall, and at the third watch of the night reached Xiaxin Dam, which was the same as the New Weir seen before. We were again hauled over the dam, passing one large bridge, with several tens of great trees standing in rows in the river. Near dawn we reached Zhong Dam, which was again the same as Xiaxin Dam. We were again hauled over and went on upstream; the river was the Shangyu River.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初三日
paragraphs.en: 3rd day

paragraphs.orig: 過上虞縣。是日睛。過二大橋而上。江之南有官人乘轎而來，乃上虞知縣自縣來也。縣距江岸二三里許。又過黃浦橋、華渡鋪、蔡墓鋪、大板橋、步青雲門、新橋鋪，至曹娥驛，驛丞徐深也。驛北有壩，舍舟過壩，步至曹娥江，亂流而渡。越岸又有壩，壩與梁湖巡檢司南北相對。又舍舟過壩，而步西二里至東關驛。復乘船，過文昌橋、東關鋪、景靈橋、黃家堰鋪、瓜山鋪、陶家堰鋪、茅洋鋪。夜四更，至一名不知江岸留泊。
paragraphs.reading: 과상우현. 시일정. 과이대교이상. 강지남유관인승교이래, 내상우지현자현래야. 현거강안이삼리허. 우과황포교, 화도포, 채묘포, 대판교, 보청운문, 신교포, 지조아역, 역승서심야. 역북유파, 사주과파, 보지조아강, 난류이도. 월안우유파, 파여양호순검사남북상대. 우사주과파, 이보서이리지동관역. 부승선, 과문창교, 동관포, 경령교, 황가언포, 과산포, 도가언포, 모양포. 야사경, 지일명부지강안류박.
paragraphs.en: Passed Shangyu County. That day fair. Passing two large bridges we went up. On the south of the river an official came by sedan chair; he was the magistrate of Shangyu, coming from the county seat. The county seat is some two or three li from the river bank. We passed also Huangpu Bridge, Huadu Post, Caimu Post, Daban Bridge, Buqingyun Gate and Xin Bridge Post, and reached Cao’e Station, where the station master was Xu Shen. North of the station was a dam; leaving the boat we crossed the dam and walked to the Cao’e River, and crossed it through the cross-currents. Across the bank was another dam, which faced the Liang Lake Inspectorate north and south. Again leaving the boat we crossed the dam and walked west two li to Dongguan Station. Again we took a boat, passing Wenchang Bridge, Dongguan Post, Jingling Bridge, Huangjiayan Post, Guashan Post, Taojiayan Post and Maoyang Post. At the fourth watch of the night we reached a river bank of unknown name and halted to moor.

paragraphs.orig: ## △初四日
paragraphs.en: 4th day

paragraphs.orig: 到紹興府。是日晴。撐鑒水而上，——水自鏡湖一派來，繞城中，——日出時，到紹興府。自城南溯鑒水而東而北，過昌安鋪棹入城。城有虹門，當水口，凡四重皆設鐵扃。過有光相橋等五大橋，及經魁門、聯桂門、祐聖觀、會水則碑，可十餘里許，有官府。翟勇引臣等下岸，其闤闠之繁、人物之盛，三倍於寧波府矣。總督備倭署都指揮僉事黃宗、巡視海道副使吳文元、布政司分守右參議陳潭，連坐於澂清堂北壁，兵甲、笞杖森列。於前置一桌，引臣至桌邊，西向而立。問以臣之姓名、所住之鄉、所筮仕之官、所漂風之故、所無登劫之情狀、所齎器械之有無。臣答以答把總官之詞，卻添載下山逢賊、仙岩遇杖之事，所齎行李又添馬鞍一部。三使相即下把總官所報狀以示臣曰：「是何供詞！前後詳略不同乎？」臣曰：「把總官初問，衹答以漂流到泊之情。今日布政三司更問，詳舉遇賊等事耳。」三使相徐謂臣曰：「供詞有違，汝實有罪。汝宜謄寫前詞，無一字加減」云云。臣便寫之。
paragraphs.reading: 도소흥부. 시일청. 탱감수이상, ——수자경호일파래, 요성중, ——일출시, 도소흥부. 자성남소감수이동이북, 과창안포도입성. 성유홍문, 당수구, 범사중개설철경. 과유광상교등오대교, 급경괴문, 연계문, 우성관, 회수칙비, 가십여리허, 유관부. 적용인신등하안, 기환궤지번, 인물지성, 삼배어영파부의. 총독비왜서도지휘첨사황종, 순시해도부사오문원, 포정사분수우참의진담, 연좌어징청당북벽, 병갑, 태장삼렬. 어전치일탁, 인신지탁변, 서향이립. 문이신지성명, 소주지향, 소서사지관, 소표풍지고, 소무등겁지정상, 소재기계지유무. 신답이답파총관지사, 각첨재하산봉적, 선암우장지사, 소재행리우첨마안일부. 삼사상즉하파총관소보상이시신왈: 「시하공사! 전후상략부동호?」신왈: 「파총관초문, 기답이표류도박지정. 금일포정삼사갱문, 상거우적등사이.」삼사상서위신왈: 「공사유위, 여실유죄. 여의등사전사, 무일자가감」운운. 신편사지.
paragraphs.en: Reached Shaoxing Prefecture. That day fair. We poled up the Jian River — the water comes as a branch from Mirror Lake and winds through the city — and at sunrise reached Shaoxing Prefecture. From south of the city we went up the Jian River east and then north, passed Chang’an Post and sculled into the city. The city had rainbow gates at the water entrance, four tiers in all, each with iron bars. We passed five large bridges including Guangxiang Bridge, and the Jingkui Gate, Liangui Gate, Youshengguan and the Huishuize stele, and after about ten li or so there was a government office. Zhai Yong led us ashore; the busyness of its market quarters and the abundance of its people were three times those of Ningbo Prefecture. The Supreme Commander for Defence against the Japanese, acting Assistant Regional Military Commissioner Huang Zong; the Vice Commissioner for Inspection of the Coastal Circuit, Wu Wenyuan; and the Divisional Right Participating Counsellor of the Provincial Administration Commission, Chen Tan, sat in a row against the north wall of Chengqing Hall, with soldiers, armour, rods and sticks ranged in ranks. In front a table was placed; I was led to the table and stood facing west. They asked me my surname and name, the district where I lived, the offices I had held, the reason for my drifting in the wind, the circumstances of my not having plundered, and whether I carried weapons. I answered with the words I had answered the Commander with, adding the matters of meeting robbers at Xiashan and being beaten at Xianyan, and adding a saddle to the baggage I carried. The three officials at once produced the report the Commander had submitted and showed me, saying: “What kind of deposition is this! Why do the earlier and later differ in detail and brevity?” I said: “When the Commander first asked, I answered only the circumstances of drifting and mooring. Today, the three offices of the Provincial Administration asking again, I have listed in detail the encounter with robbers and the like.” The three officials said slowly: “The deposition differs; you are indeed guilty. You must copy out the earlier statement without adding or removing a single character,” and so on. I wrote it at once.

paragraphs.orig: 三使相又謂臣曰：「他日你到杭州鎮守太監繡衣三司大人，到北京兵部、禮部，亦更問汝情，其亦以是答之。少有相違大不可也！」又問曰：「初以汝類為倭船劫掠，將加捕戮。汝若是朝鮮人，汝國歷代沿革、都邑、山川、人物、俗尚、祀典、喪制、戶口、兵制、田賦、冠裳之制，仔細寫來，質之諸史，以考是非。」臣曰：「沿革、都邑：則初檀君，與唐堯並立，國號朝鮮，都平壤，歷世千有餘年。周武王封箕子於朝鮮，都平壤，以八條教民，今國人以禮義成俗始此。厥後，燕人衛滿亡命入朝鮮，逐箕子之後箕準，準奔馬韓以都焉。其間，或為九韓，或為二府，或為四郡，或為三韓，年代久遠，不能盡述。至西漢宣帝時，新羅朴氏初立國，高句麗高氏、百濟扶餘氏相繼而起，三分舊朝鮮之地。新羅據東南界，都慶州陋；高句麗據西北界，都遼東，都平壤，又屢遷厥邦，忘其地；百濟據中西南界，都稷山，都廣州，都漢陽，都公州，都扶餘。當唐高宗朝，新羅文武王與唐兵滅高句麗，又滅百濟，合三國為一。後，甄萱叛據全州，弓裔叛據鐵原。高麗王氏功高德盛，國人推戴，弓裔自竄，甄萱自投，新羅王封府庫籍郡縣來降，再合三國，都開城，傳世幾五百年。今革為我朝鮮，都漢陽，蓋將百年於茲矣。山川：則長白山在東北，一名白頭山，橫亙千餘里，高二百餘里，其巔有潭，周八十餘里。東流為豆滿江，南流為鴨綠江，東北流為速平江，西北流為松花江，松花下流即混同江也；妙香山在北；金剛山在東，有一萬二千餘峰；智異山在南；九月山在西。右四山極高峻，多奇跡。三角山，即國都鎮山。大同江、薩水、臨津渡、漢江、洛東江、熊津、豆恥津、榮山津，已上川之大者。人物：則新羅金庚信、金陽、崔致遠、薛聰；百濟階伯；高句麗乙支文德；高麗崔衝、姜邯讚、趙衝、金就礪、禹倬、鄭夢周；我朝鮮不可歷數。俗尚，則尚禮義，明五倫，重儒術；每春秋行養老宴、鄉射禮、鄉飲酒禮。祀典，則社稷、宗廟，釋奠諸山川。刑制，從《大明律》。喪制，從朱子《家禮》。冠裳，遵華制。戶口、兵制、田賦，我以儒臣未知其詳。」又問曰：「所謂推刷人丁，何事？」臣曰：「濟州在大海中，水路甚險甚遠。凡有犯罪者，皆逃入以避，久為逋逃之藪，故往刷之。」又問曰：「濟州距我中國幾里？」臣虛張水路之遠，曰：「不可知其詳也。大抵船遇便風於大海，則日可行千里。今我自濟州浮海，折晝夜則凡二十九日，為大風所驅，疾行如飛，到泊於中國海岸。則自中國距濟州路，大概數萬餘里矣。」又問曰：「汝國與我朝廷相距遠近幾何？」臣曰：「傳聞自我國都過鴨綠江，經遼東城抵皇都，三千九百有餘里。」總兵官三使相即饋臣以茶果，仍書單字以賜。
paragraphs.reading: 삼사상우위신왈: 「타일이도항주진수태감수의삼사대인, 도북경병부, 예부, 역갱문여정, 기역이시답지. 소유상위대불가야!」우문왈: 「초이여류위왜선겁략, 장가포륙. 여약시조선인, 여국역대연혁, 도읍, 산천, 인물, 속상, 사전, 상제, 호구, 병제, 전부, 관상지제, 자세사래, 질지제사, 이고시비.」신왈: 「연혁, 도읍: 칙초단군, 여당요병립, 국호조선, 도평양, 역세천유여년. 주무왕봉기자어조선, 도평양, 이팔조교민, 금국인이예의성속시차. 궐후, 연인위만망명입조선, 축기자지후기준, 준분마한이도언. 기간, 혹위구한, 혹위이부, 혹위사군, 혹위삼한, 연대구원, 불능진술. 지서한선제시, 신라박씨초립국, 고구려고씨, 백제부여씨상계이기, 삼분구조선지지. 신라거동남계, 도경주루; 고구려거서북계, 도요동, 도평양, 우누천궐방, 망기지; 백제거중서남계, 도직산, 도광주, 도한양, 도공주, 도부여. 당당고종조, 신라문무왕여당병멸고구려, 우멸백제, 합삼국위일. 후, 견훤반거전주, 궁예반거철원. 고려왕씨공고덕성, 국인추대, 궁예자찬, 견훤자투, 신라왕봉부고적군현내항, 재합삼국, 도개성, 전세기오백년. 금혁위아조선, 도한양, 개장백년어자의. 산천: 칙장백산재동북, 일명백두산, 횡긍천여리, 고이백여리, 기전유담, 주팔십여리. 동류위두만강, 남류위압록강, 동북류위속평강, 서북류위송화강, 송화하류즉혼동강야; 묘향산재북; 금강산재동, 유일만이천여봉; 지이산재남; 구월산재서. 우사산극고준, 다기적. 삼각산, 즉국도진산. 대동강, 살수, 임진도, 한강, 낙동강, 웅진, 두치진, 영산진, 이상천지대자. 인물: 칙신라김경신, 김양, 최치원, 설총; 백제계백; 고구려을지문덕; 고려최충, 강감찬, 조충, 김취려, 우탁, 정몽주; 아조선불가역수. 속상, 칙상예의, 명오륜, 중유술; 매춘추행양로연, 향사례, 향음주례. 사전, 칙사직, 종묘, 석전제산천. 형제, 종《대명률》. 상제, 종주자《가례》. 관상, 준화제. 호구, 병제, 전부, 아이유신미지기상.」우문왈: 「소위추쇄인정, 하사?」신왈: 「제주재대해중, 수로심험심원. 범유범죄자, 개도입이피, 구위포도지수, 고왕쇄지.」우문왈: 「제주거아중국기리?」신허장수로지원, 왈: 「불가지기상야. 대저선우편풍어대해, 칙일가행천리. 금아자제주부해, 절주야칙범이십구일, 위대풍소구, 질행여비, 도박어중국해안. 칙자중국거제주로, 대개수만여리의.」우문왈: 「여국여아조정상거원근기하?」신왈: 「전문자아국도과압록강, 경요동성저황도, 삼천구백유여리.」총병관삼사상즉궤신이다과, 잉서단자이사.
paragraphs.en: The three officials again said to me: “Another day, when you reach the Grand Defender-Eunuch at Hangzhou and the Embroidered-Robe three offices, and in Beijing the Ministry of War and the Ministry of Rites, they too will question you again on your circumstances; answer them in this same way too. Any divergence will be very bad!” They asked further: “At first we took your kind to be a plundering Japanese ship and were going to arrest and execute you. If you are indeed a Joseon person, write out in detail your country’s successive history, capitals, mountains and rivers, people, customs, sacrificial rites, mourning system, population, military system, land taxes and system of dress, to be checked against the histories to determine right and wrong.” I said: “As to history and capitals: at the beginning Dangun stood alongside Emperor Yao of Tang, the country was named Joseon, and the capital was Pyeongyang, passing more than a thousand years. King Wu of Zhou enfeoffed Gija in Joseon, with the capital at Pyeongyang, and he taught the people by eight articles; that the people of our country now have become accustomed to ritual and righteousness begins with this. Afterward, Wi Man of Yan fled to Joseon and expelled Gija’s descendant Gijun; Jun fled to Mahan and made his capital there. In the interval it was sometimes the nine Han, sometimes two prefectures, sometimes four commanderies, sometimes the three Han; the ages are long past and cannot be fully told. In the time of Emperor Xuan of Western Han, Bak of Silla first founded his country, and Go of Goguryeo and Buyeo of Baekje arose in succession, dividing the old land of Joseon into three. Silla held the south-eastern region, with its capital at Gyeongju; Goguryeo held the north-west, with capitals at Liaodong and Pyeongyang, and moved its capital repeatedly — I have forgotten the places; Baekje held the central west and south, with capitals at Jiksan, Gwangju, Hanyang, Gongju and Buyeo. In the reign of Gaozong of Tang, King Munmu of Silla with Tang troops destroyed Goguryeo and again destroyed Baekje, uniting the three states as one. Later Gyeon Hwon rebelled and occupied Jeonju, and Gungye rebelled and occupied Cheorwon. King Wang of Goryeo, high in merit and rich in virtue, was acclaimed by the people; Gungye fled of himself, Gyeon Hwon surrendered of himself, and the king of Silla, sealing up the treasuries and registers of the prefectures and counties, came to submit; the three states were united a second time, the capital was at Gaeseong, and it was passed on for nearly five hundred years. Now it has been changed into our Joseon, with the capital at Hanyang, and it will soon be a hundred years. As to mountains and rivers: Mt. Jangbaek is in the north-east, also called Mt. Baekdu, stretching across more than a thousand li, more than two hundred li high; at its summit is a lake, over eighty li in circumference. Flowing east it becomes the Duman River, flowing south the Amnok River, flowing north-east the Sokpyeong River, flowing north-west the Songhua River; the lower Songhua is the Huntong River. Mt. Myohyang is in the north; Mt. Geumgang in the east, with more than twelve thousand peaks; Mt. Jiri in the south; Mt. Gumwol in the west. These four mountains are very lofty and have many wonders. Mt. Samgak is the guardian mountain of the capital. The Daedong River, the Sal River, the Imjin crossing, the Han River, the Nakdong River, Ungjin, Duchi Ford and Yeongsan Ford are the great rivers. As to people: of Silla, Kim Yusin, Kim Yang, Choe Chiwon, Seol Chong; of Baekje, Gyebaek; of Goguryeo, Eulji Mundeok; of Goryeo, Choe Chung, Gang Gamchan, Jo Chung, Kim Chwiryeo, U Tak, Jeong Mongju; those of our Joseon cannot be counted. As to customs, we honour ritual and righteousness, make clear the five relationships, and value Confucian learning; every spring and autumn we hold feasts for the aged, the district archery rite and the district wine-drinking rite. As to sacrificial rites: the altars of the soil and grain, the ancestral temple, and the sacrifice to Confucius, and those to the mountains and rivers. The penal system follows the Great Ming Code. The mourning system follows Zhu Xi’s Family Rites. Dress follows the Chinese system. As to population, military system and land taxes, as a Confucian official I do not know the details.” They asked again: “What was this ‘investigating and registering people’ you spoke of?” I said: “Jeju is in the great sea and the sea route is very dangerous and very far. All who commit crimes flee into it to escape, and it has long been a haunt of fugitives, so I went to investigate and register them.” They asked again: “How far is Jeju from our China?” I exaggerated the distance of the sea route, and said: “I cannot know in detail. Generally a boat meeting a favourable wind on the great sea can go a thousand li in a day. Now I floated from Jeju, counting day and night separately, twenty-nine in all, driven by a great wind, running like flying, and anchored on the Chinese coast. So the route from China to Jeju is generally tens of thousands of li.” They asked again: “How far is your country from our court?” I said: “I have heard that from our capital across the Amnok River, passing through the city of Liaodong, to the imperial capital is over three thousand nine hundred li.” The three officials, the Commander-in-Chief, at once gave me tea and fruit, and also wrote a list and gave it to me.

paragraphs.orig: 單字中送崔官禮物：豬肉一盤，鵝二隻，雞四翼，魚二尾，酒一樽，米一盤，胡桃一盤，菜一盤，筍一盤，麵筋一盤，棗一盤，豆腐一盤。又賜饌糧等物於陪吏、軍人有差。臣即做謝詩再拜。三使相亦起答禮致恭。又謂臣曰：「看汝謝詩，此地方山川汝何知之詳？必此地人所說。」臣曰：「四顧無親，語音不通，誰與話言，我嘗閱中國地圖，到此臆記耳。」對畢，臣與三四官人拱立桌邊。有翟勇之軍吏一人，在外頭毆打臣之從者金都終，有傷。臣寫以示諸官人，一官人奔告於總兵官。總兵官拿其毆打人，治罪杖之，又杖勇以不能馭下之罪。臣等退，復沿湖棹出城外，過迎恩橋，至蓬萊驛前留泊。夕，知府——姓周——及會稽、山陰兩縣官，皆優送糧饌。

paragraphs.en: In the list: gifts sent to the official Choe — pork, one plate; geese, two; chickens, four; fish, two; wine, one jar; rice, one plate; walnuts, one plate; vegetables, one plate; bamboo shoots, one plate; wheat gluten, one plate; jujubes, one plate; tofu, one plate. They also gave food and grain and the like to the attendant clerks and the soldiers, in varying amounts. I at once composed a poem of thanks and bowed twice. The three officials also rose and returned the courtesy with respect. They said to me again: “Looking at your poem of thanks, how do you know this region’s mountains and rivers in such detail? It must have been told by people of this place.” I said: “I looked in all four directions and had no relatives, and our speech is not understood; with whom could I have talked? I once looked at a map of China, and what I recorded here was from memory, by guesswork.” When the answers were finished, I stood with hands clasped at the table’s edge with three or four officials. One military clerk of Zhai Yong, outside, beat my follower Kim Dojong and injured him. I wrote it to show the officials, and one official ran to inform the Commander-in-Chief. The Commander-in-Chief seized the man who had beaten him and punished him with the rod, and also beat Yong for the fault of being unable to control his subordinates. We withdrew, and again along the lake sculled out of the city, passing Ying’en Bridge, and halted at the front of Penglai Station. In the evening the prefect — surnamed Zhou — and the officials of Kuaiji and Shanyin counties all sent grain and provisions generously.
